Three Nigerian nationals have been killed in recent weeks in South Africa, Nigerian authorities said Tuesday, adding to tensions between the two countries over persistent violence against migrants.

Nigeria's ambassador-designate to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, said the three were killed between Sept. 18 and 21. He identified them as Kenechukwu Christopher Igwemmadu, killed in Bloemfontein; Olaniyi Olaleye Olatunde, in Pretoria, and Christian Hillary Nnaemeka, in Primrose.

The deaths bring the number of Nigerians killed in South Africa this year to 12 and 112 since 2022, the Nigerian official said.

“Nigeria will protect its nationals,” Fani-Kayode wrote on the social platform X.

South Africa has been rocked in recent months by violent anti-migrant protests that have forced thousands of migrants to leave and caused diplomatic tensions with other African nations. Earlier this month, Nigeria’s parliament indefinitely suspended official visits and engagements with South Africa over the violence.

The Nigerian consulate in South Africa said Tuesday that the recent deaths of the three Nigerians “coming in quick succession, also raise questions about what seems to be a pattern of targeting Nigerians in South Africa.”

South African authorities did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

“We continue to call on relevant South African authorities to investigate the deaths thoroughly and bring the perpetrators of the gruesome acts to justice,” said consul-general Ninikanwa Okey-Uche in a statement.

South Africa has for years attracted foreign nationals from across the continent, including many from Nigeria, seeking economic opportunities. Foreigners have also experienced sporadic outbursts of xenophobic violence. Protesters blame them for the country's high levels of unemployment, crime and pressure on public services.

In June, two Nigerians were killed during anti-migrant violence in South Africa, just two days before an unofficial deadline set by protesters for foreigners to leave. Nigeria’s foreign ministry said one was allegedly killed by police officers and the other by unidentified attackers.

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

Sports.title: ‘Can’t be bullied by a young kid’ – Rio Ferdinand urges Man Utd to be ‘strong’ over shock JJ Gabriel transfer saga
Sports.content:
Next

RIO FERDINAND is calling on Manchester United to harden their stance against wantaway starlet JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel, 15, is seeking an escape route out of Old Trafford after revealing his intention to leave the club, and has been linked with moves to some of Europe’s biggest sides.



United sources do not expect Gabriel to show his face at the club again after he asked them to de-register him.

Gabriel has been with United since the age of 11 and his potential has seen him nicknamed “Kid Messi”.



Despite not turning 16 until October 6, Gabriel believes he can make better progress elsewhere and will certainly not be short options if he leaves the club.

But Ferdinand issued a warning to his former club and insists that United must do all they can within their power to keep the forward.



He said on his YouTube channel: “I just feel that Man United can’t be seen to be bullied by a young kid who is 15 years old, no matter how good he is.

“So whatever the outcome is, Man United have to remain strong in this until the end because whatever the decision or whatever way this plays out, there will be kids coming after this who will be using it as a reference point and you can’t be seen to be weak in this situation as a football club.

“But I’m not going to sit here and hammer on the kid or pick apart what’s going on because I don’t have the facts around how they’ve got to this situation, this end point, that JJ Gabriel and his family are demanding to leave.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ferdinand also hailed the player’s undoubted potential, and added: “It’s crazy. I don’t know where this kid’s ceiling is. I’ve seen him play, I’ve seen him train, I’ve listened to people who have coached him for a number of years and there’s no doubt this kid is going to the top.”



United – who are already looking at another wonderkid to sign as a replacement – are certainly in a strong position to keep the youngster for now at least, and can challenge Gabriel’s request to terminate his current terms.

Premier League rules stipulate as follows: “During your child’s registration period, their registration may only be cancelled if everyone agrees (the club, player and their parent/carer).”

That has not stopped Gabriel’s agent Ali Barat from engineering Gabriel’s next move, with talks having already been arranged with Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

The ugly fallout certainly seems set to continue for a while longer, with Gabriel removing all pictures linking him to United from his social media – before reuploading some.

It is a troubling situation for boss Michael Carrick, but his main focus will be on their next Premier League game against Tottenham on October 10.

Sports.title: Dark history of one of biggest sports stadium ever that hosted Hitler’s birthday celebrations before being left to rot
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND are set to face the Czech Republic only TEN miles down the road from the stadium where Adolf Hitler celebrated his 50th birthday.

Slavia Prague’s Fortuna Arena will host the Three Lions in their Nations League battle tonight, which despite its capacity of 19,000 is now the country’s biggest ground.



The Great Strahov Stadium can be spotted from the heavens of this evening’s ground – but the dark history of what was once the world’s biggest stadium is not so obvious.

The huge arena, overlooking the old city, could hold up to 250,000 in its heyday.



Originally, the site hosted colossal gymnastics events with the 63,500 square-metre field large – enough space to park 2,300 double-decker buses.

In 1933, the stadium – which is only beaten for size by the 257,000 Indianapolis Motor Speedway – hosted its first motorcycle speedway.

Mammoth anti-war demonstrations were held within the grounds in 1938, drawing nearly 350,000 people.

But in a peculiar turn of events, Hitler took it over to celebrate his 50th birthday with a parade of honour.

It was also used as an assembly point before Jewish people were sent to concentration camps.

Then after WWII, it was turned into a temporary detention centre before German-speaking Czechs were expelled.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Even after the war, the US Army played a game of American football.

In the 1990s, the likes of The Rolling Stones, Guns N’ Roses, Bon Jovi and Pink Floyd took over the roaring venue, attracting hundreds of thousands of music fans.



And in 1995, Pope John Paul II used it for a huge public mass.

In the decade following, AC/DC and Ozzfest with Ozzy Osbourne, Tool and Slayer kept it on the Prague map.

As the years crept on, its immense size made it too difficult to look after and it fell into disrepair.

Maintenance proved costly and difficult but it has been SAVED.

It reportedly became a UNESCO Heritage Site in 2003, ruling out any potential demolition discussions and raising the question, “What next?”.



Now it has been converted by Czech giants Slavia Prague into their training ground that features eight stunning pitches within the crumbling ruins.

Even West Ham benefited from the pitches at one point after they were loaned to the Championship club to aid with their 2023 Conference League final clash at the Fortuna Arena.



Jarrod Bowen netted the winner in the 2-1 box office win over Serie A side Fiorentina.

Only three of the starting XI remain at the club, with the likes of Declan Rice, who captained the Hammers on the night, departing.

While the pitches have a close eye kept on them, the audience accommodation continues to dwindle into ruin with the lack of fans turning up.

And to add to it, the terraces have been ruled unsafe, with it far from likely that they would be able to hold a crowd anywhere near what it used to.

But the future of the stadium remains dependent on the club, with any potential redevelopment running a risk with its historical significance.



And even opposite the Strahov land comes ANOTHER huge stadium – only 300 seats smaller than the Fortuna Arena.

OLIVIER GIROUD looks set to pull the curtain down on his trophy-laden career.

Giroud, who turns 40 this week, dropped the strongest hint yet that he will be hanging his boots up at the end of this season in an interview with French newspaper L’Équipe.



Giroud was recounting his career at the highest level, and was best known on these shores for his spells at Arsenal and Chelsea.

He said: “We can do interviews for L’Équipe next year, with pleasure, but as a player, I think this is very likely my last season. That’s why I’m enjoying every moment.”



The striker arrived at Arsenal from Montpellier in June 2012, scoring 105 goals in 253 appearances.

He won three FA Cups at the Emirates, before crossing London to join Chelsea in January 2018.



He lifted another FA Cup at the Blues, before winning the Europa League and Champions League in 2019 and 2021 respectively.

Giroud was an unused substitute in that Champions League final win for Chelsea against Manchester City, and joined AC Milan the summer.

He added a Serie A winners’ medal to his trophy cabinet in 2022, and became France’s record goalscorer at the 2022 World Cup, in a 3-1 win over Poland.

Kylian Mbappe broke Giroud’s record at the 2026 finals by netting a double in a 3-1 World Cup win over Senegal.

Gabby Agbonlahor has pulled no punches after Manchester City’s guilty verdict by jokingly asking a handful of his old team-mates to hand back their medals.

Man City battle with Premier League will take ‘a lot more time’ says Ferran Soriano

Manchester City were alerted to their guilty verdict regarding 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules before a summer of big spending, it is claimed. The Cityzens have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they were slapped with in 2023, with the news breaking on Friday afternoon.

‌



However, as per ESPN, sources say that City learned their fate months ago. The publication has been told that executives at City were initially made aware of the independent panel's verdict back in July, with the club still investing massively in their first-team afterwards.

‌



In total, seven senior signings arrived at the Etihad Stadium, totalling a staggering £450million, following the verdict - if the sources' claims ring true. "They must have been talking about something to do with them at school and they was like, 'Can you go into the shop?' They gave me money and was like, 'Can you get the Lucozade?' They gave me money. I was just sat in the back, I didn't get out of the car.

"Thirty seconds went by and they looked back, they're still talking. They look back and they was like, 'Can you go get the Lucozades?' I was like, 'I can't'. They was like, 'Why?' I was like, 'I'm banned for life."

‌



Dele Alli makes another return to Tottenham as star eyes contract READ MORE :

Asked by the interviewer why and what he stole, he added: "Because I was robbing the place up. Everything bro."

Tesco has been contacted for comment.

Alli, a star of England's run to the semi-final of the 2018 World Cup, left Spurs in 2022 and has since struggled to rebuild his career. After failed spells at Everton, Besiktas (on loan) and Como, the 30-year-old is a free agent.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

He spent time training at Spurs last season to build up his fitness. This season, he has been training at the home of League Two side Barnet, sharing a video of him in shooting practice at the north London side's The Hive base.

He has since been invited to formally train with the Bees, who currently top League Two. Barnet boss Dean Brennan says he would love to sign the midfielder, telling The Sun: "If my owner said to me, 'You could sign Dele Alli', I'd run the London Marathon for him – even though I haven't run for about 20 years! Whatever I had to do to sign Dele Alli, I'd take it because he is a fantastic talent.

‌



View 2 Images Como were Alli's last club (Image: Jonathan Moscrop/Getty Images)

"He has got himself into a situation where things haven't worked out how they should, but that's life. I know Mauricio Pochettino and Karl Robinson, who managed him at MK Dons, thought he was a special talent.

"He still has that special quality but football moves so fast and the game's not showing him any love. I'd absolutely snap your hands off if Dele was interested and take him all day long. We'll see what happens."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney shows his true colours with response to Man City being stripped of titles
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney shows his true colours with response to Man City being stripped of titles

Manchester United are one of the clubs which could be given an extra Premier League title should Manchester City be stripped of their crowns after being found guilty of financial breaches

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney has disagreed with two ex-team-mates (Image: The Overlap)

Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney says that he would NOT accept a Premier League winners' medal if Manchester City are stripped of their 2012 title win. Rooney, 40, admits that he'd be 'uncomfortable' being awarded a medal after United finished second to City and lost the title on goal difference.

‌



It was City's first Premier League crown, with Sergio Aguero scoring the iconic stoppage-time winner on the final day. But Rooney's stance goes against two of his former team-mates.

‌



Both Rio Ferdinand and David de Gea have suggested that they should be considered title winners from the 2011-12 season after City were found to have breached financial rules between 2009 and 2018. The club continue to deny the 115 charges and say that they remain confident they'll prove their innocence.

‌



"I have heard Rio has come out saying about getting another Premier League medal... I wouldn't really feel comfortable accepting another Premier League medal, if I'm being honest," Rooney said on the Stick To United podcast.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I don't think we deserve it, we didn't do enough that season to win the league. I think we were six or seven points clear with four or five games to go and we threw it away.

"I've seen everything that has come out over the past few days and listening to people and I was putting myself in a Man City player's shoes... they're players, they're doing everything they can to try and win the Premier League title and in their mind they have done it, if those players have no understanding of what is going on above them, if that happened to me... I would be absolutely devastated.

Should Manchester City be stripped of their titles? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City denied Manchester Unted the title in 2012 (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

"It might happen, they might take them [medals] away, but I wouldn't want it [a medal] because I don't think as a team we deserved it that year because obviously we didn't finish first.

"So when I see team-mates saying, 'I want a medal', I'm happy with the five I've won. I wouldn't want this one. Should they get it stripped for what the owners have done? Yeah maybe, but I wouldn't feel comfortable accepting it."

‌



The Premier League haven't issued a statement on the verdict, with reports first emerging on Friday. The league have, however, declined to comment while City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak addressed the reports in a letter to fans on Saturday.

Al Mubarak wrote: "The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began. There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position.

Sports.title: Norway boss erupts over Erling Haaland 'lies' after Man City 115 charges verdict
Sports.content:
Norway boss erupts over Erling Haaland 'lies' after Man City 115 charges verdict

Manchester City and Norway striker Erling Haaland has the support of his national team head coach following a press conference U-turn

View 2 Images Erling Haaland 'lies' have been slammed by Norway head coach Stale Solbakken (Image: (Photo by Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

The Erling Haaland press conference saga has taken a fresh twist with head coach Stale Solbakken firing back at claims Manchester City made the decision. Their striker was due to face questions from reporters ahead of a Nations League game against Portugal, but the national team reversed that decision.

‌



Those press duties were due to take place on Saturday, less than 24 hours after City's guilty verdict over 114 alleged financial breaches, but he was replaced by Fredrik Aursnes and Andreas Schjelderup.

‌



Solbakken confirmed in his pre-match press conference that he was involved in the decision, and he has since angrily revealed, after the 2-1 defeat to Portugal, that Man City made no request to have Haaland away from journalists.

‌



"I haven't spoken to anyone at Manchester City about the media since Erling was to move from Dortmund to City," he admitted to VG, via Sport Witness: "That was the last time I spoke to City about the media.

"It's a lie. It also undermines my integrity. I go to great lengths to be honest because this is the people's national team. I try to give my all and that of the team. This was a decision I made [giving him a day off on Saturday] without informing Erling. I just said: 'You can let this go. If you want to go, then you go. But for me you are exempt'."

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



There had been claims in Norway that City made the final decision on Haaland's availability for the press conference, but those have been firmly shot down by Solbakken.

The Norway boss has also attempted to play down the City charges - which continue to be denied by the club - and its potential impact on Haaland, having stated he should be focused on scoring goals, and he did exactly that on Sunday evening.

Haaland fired home a rebound early into the second half, but Portugal still came out winners in Oslo. He was directly up against City team-mate Ruben Dias, with the pair spotted in discussion after the game.

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland was up against Manchester City team-mate Ruben Dias

The Norwegian striker didn't extend the same warmth towards former City colleague Bernardo Silva, with cameras capturing only the briefest of interactions between them.

Silva actually moved in for an embrace but appeared to be rebuffed by Haaland. Frustration over the result might explain that reaction, or perhaps simply because they're no longer club colleagues.

Article continues below

Some observers have also pointed to the Real Madrid star's extremely late challenge on Martin Odegaard as a potential source of Haaland's irritation. Despite the threat of a points deduction hanging over them, other City players appear concentrated on their duties by also making their mark at international level.

Rayan Cherki provided an assist from the bench for France as they secured a late victory over Belgium on Monday. Last week, Nico O'Reilly also delivered the cross that Harry Kane nodded home via Marc Cucurella.

Later in that match against Spain, it was O'Reilly who surrendered possession in a dangerous position, allowing Alex Baena to score shortly afterwards. Marc Guehi also committed an individual mistake that Lamine Yamal capitalised on during the opening period.

Sports.title: World's largest abandoned stadium with 250,000 capacity left to rot in Czech Republic
Sports.content:
World's largest abandoned stadium with 250,000 capacity left to rot in Czech Republic

A ground a few miles away from where the Czech Republic will face England has been reclaimed by nature

View 3 Images The Great Strahov Stadium is five miles from where England will face the Czech Republic (Image: Getty Images)

England will face the Czech Republic in a modest stadium just miles from a venue that once held 250,000. Prague's Fortuna Arena will host Thomas Tuchel's side as they look to bounce back from Saturday's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley.

‌



With its capacity of just under 20,000, demand has predictably outstripped supply. That wouldn't have been the case at the iconic Great Strahov Stadium, which overlooks the city's old town, a couple of miles from the new city centre.

‌



Built in 1926, the venue was first used to host mass synchronised gymnastics displays before being repurposed in various ways over the years. For public events, it could once accommodate a quarter of a million spectators.

‌



With a sitting capacity of around 56,000, that would have been reduced for sports like football but still far superior to the Fortuna Arena. The ground would need a lick of paint, though, as the stands have been left to rot and reclaimed by nature, having not hosted competitive sport since 2019.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

However, it is still used. The ground has been a training base for Sparta Prague in recent times, with West Ham paying a visit ahead of their victory in the 2023 Europa Conference League title. Its vast playing area can accommodate eight full-size football pitches, plus a couple of futsal pitches.

‌



England injury blow confirmed as Thomas Tuchel names squad for Czechia clash READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel makes Jude Bellingham feelings crystal clear after Spain show READ MORE :

The complex is owned by the City of Prague, which may be considering what to do with the vast area. Some traditionalists will want it to remain associated with sport and potentially transform it into a modern venue, while others will see it as prime real estate.

That will be the least of Tuchel's worries as he looks to avoid England sliding into a post-World Cup hangover. While there were positives from the defeat to Spain, the defence was a real area of concern.

View 3 Images While the pitches are in pristine conditions, the stands at Great Strahov Stadium have been left to decay (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Tuchel admits the loss to Spain "puts a bit of pressure" on England but is "nothing we can't handle" ahead of facing the side ranked 49th in the world. He said: "It's a bit early for a 'must win', a bit early in the group for a 'must win'. We always arrive at every match, preparing the team with a target to win.

"It's always the target, it was the target against Spain, it will be the target [against the Czechs]. We respect the opposition, respect their quality, respect the challenge it brings.

View 3 Images The Fortuna Arena, where England will play, has a capacity of 19,300 (Image: Alex Grimm/Getty Images)

Article continues below

"If you play in Prague against Czechia, it will be difficult, it will be emotional, with the support for home team being what it is.

"Like I said, we always prepare for a win, we want the win, but in the [context] of the group, knowing where we want to go, it’s too early to speak of a 'must win'. It would be ideal, but the problem is the opposition on the other side."

Sports.title: Paul Scholes backs Erling Haaland to STRUGGLE in League Two as Man City await punishment
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes backs Erling Haaland to STRUGGLE in League Two as Man City await punishment

Manchester City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules last week, with calls for the club to be relegated landing as a result

View 2 Images Paul Scholes has spoken about Manchester City's charges saga (Image: YouTube / The Good, The Bad and The Football)

Paul Scholes believes that Erling Haaland would struggle to score goals in League Two, in the hypothetical scenario that Manchester City are relegated from the Premier League. The club received a guilty verdict on 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules on Friday, following a three-year investigation.

‌



As a result, players, pundits, managers and fans have speculated what punishment should be handed to City for the infractions, which are claimed to have taken place over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. While slaps on the wrist like fines and transfer embargoes have been floated around, more extreme punishments that the club could face include points deductions, being stripped of their titles and even relegation from the English top flight.

‌



In the latest instalment of the Good, the Bad and the Football, Scholes, Paddy McGuinness, Nicky Butt and Mark Ogden discussed the City saga, as well as the longshot prospect of City playing League Two football next season through demotion.

‌



McGuinness said: "Hypotheticals, a bit of fun. Let's say City get relegated to League Two. In League Two, because obviously it's a different game down there, how many goals a season does Haaland score?"

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



While Butt was quick to reply: "None, cause he won't be there," Scholes was happier to entertain McGuinness. He explained: "In all honesty, we'll never know. But it'd be very difficult, it's a different game."

McGuinness then added: "Could he go and get 100 goals? I don't think he would in League Two," with Scholes responding: "He'd get a few at home - at the away grounds I don't think it'd be easy," adding: "He probably wouldn't play a lot of games. He'd probably be injured for quite a few, I would have thought."

When probed how many goals he'd score, Scholes continued: "He'd be alright up until the pitches are good in October, and then he'll be fine again from March to May. It's just that little November to February time it might be a bit difficult."

‌



Any respective punishment may have to wait a little while longer, however, as a result of City being all but certain to appeal Friday's verdict from an independent panel. That's given the club have claimed innocence since being slapped with the charges in 2023.

View 2 Images Erling Haaland has been vital to Manchester City's recent success (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

City chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, shared an open letter with fans on Saturday in the wake of the reported verdict, thanking them for sticking by the club while explaining that they will continue to fight their corner. CEO, Ferran Soriano, meanwhile, attended a meeting in Copenhagen with Premier League officials earlier this week.

Article continues below

There it is reported that he told the room: "It has taken eight years to reach this point and it will still take much more time," before dodging media questions in the aftermath. As the Premier League will wait to conclude the case before deciding on respective punishment, it could be a while until football fans learn the definitive outcome of the investigation.

The Premier League are yet to publicly comment since the news emerged on Friday, as a result of privacy and confidentiality laws.

Sports.title: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role
Sports.content:
Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.

McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July, with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor, but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats.

That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka, raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McCullum has remained in charge of England's white-ball teams, alongside specialist mentor Kevin Pietersen

Buttler, who captained the team in their ill-fated 2023 title defence, thinks the split coaching model has allowed McCullum to throw all his energy towards next year's tournament in southern Africa.

"He's only got one focus now and that is the white ball," Buttler said on his For the Love of Cricket podcast.

"It's not that he couldn't do everything, because he could, but your time is more spread and you've got more to think about with the Test team as well.

"Now he can focus solely on white-ball cricket - T20, yes, but mainly ODI cricket with that World Cup on the horizon. It seems like Baz is naturally all in on, 'how do I win this World Cup with this team?'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Buttler said McCullum now has more time to focus on the white-ball format

"I think he can sort of see that World Cup is not that far away. It's a real target, now his remit has changed from four months ago being in charge of everything to, 'right, I can really nail down on this'. He's just got more time and more focus on that.

"ODI cricket for England has not been consistently great for a couple of years, so there's some nice growth to go on that and this summer's been a really good start."

Buttler delivers update on hamstring injury

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Buttler was forced to retire after suffering a hamstring injury during England's second ODI against Sri Lanka

Buttler is currently sidelined with a hamstring injury and has already been ruled out for the forthcoming tri-series tour of Pakistan.

He is also a doubt for the November trip to Australia, meaning the team's most experienced one-day player could miss as many as eight ODIs and a significant chunk of the pre-World Cup preparations.

"I've had a scan and I'm waiting to see the specialist. Then we'll know what the next steps are," he said.

"The unknown is often the tough part. Any cricketer just wants a physio or a doctor to tell you, 'on this date you'll be back playing cricket'. Unfortunately, they can't do that just yet."

Sports.title: The NFL returns to the UK - will we soon see a European franchise?
Sports.content:
The NFL returns to the United Kingdom this weekend with the first of three London games to be played in the month of October.

We'll see the Indianapolis Colts take on the Washington Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday and the following week we will welcome back the Jacksonville Jaguars as they clash with the Philadelphia Eagles at the same venue.

The trio of games will end at Wembley Stadium on October 18 with the Jags taking on their division rivals in the AFC South in the Houston Texans.

The NFL continues its commitment to the UK but it's clear they are looking more globally than ever before. By the end of this 2026 season we will have seen nine regular season games played internationally and the NFL is growing braver.

I think London played a big part in that as well by proving time and time again how you can get teams in, get them practising efficiently, get them playing the game and then get them out.

That blueprint has now been taken quite literally to the other side of the world. So this season we'll see firsts with games already played in Australia and in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil. We'll also see a first this year with a game in Paris, France towards the end of October.

So this NFL train is not slowing down. In fact it's only going to gather pace. I think we'll see 10 games played next season and I don't think we're very far away from seeing 16 being played internationally every year.

That of course will come once the league negotiates any new deal with the Players Association that takes the regular season up to 18 games from its current 17 right now. So at first glance the league is intent on continuing with its Formula 1 approach. Different teams playing in different markets, growing the fanbase around the entire world and I understand why.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Baltimore Ravens had just seven seconds to work with at the start of their drive - which proved to be just long enough to win the game in Brazil against the Dallas Cowboys

I've spoken to NFL commissioner Roger Goodell about this in the past and he's told me that if we play in just one or two markets you only grow the fanbase in one or two markets. If you can play in 10, 11, 12 markets around the world then you're growing significantly in a number of different countries, so it certainly looks like that's the plan, but we still hear this talk of international franchises, potentially even a European division and the commissioner himself alluded to that this summer when in Germany.

I think the reason for that is that the NFL just doesn't want to lose momentum. So they are keeping an open mind. Yes at the moment it's the Formula 1 approach but if it works well enough in enough countries then does it become something else? Does it become something more substantial in London? Do we have a European division with a team in London, one in Germany, one in Spain, one in France?

When you look at it you can see the groundwork being laid for that.

I think if I were a betting man I wouldn't necessarily know which way to go. I've seen very early on a lot of talk about a franchise, especially in London, then that went away to a degree and we looked at this Formula 1 approach of different teams in different countries.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Baltimore Ravens at the Dallas Cowboys from Week 3 of the NFL season

But now the commissioner has put the franchise discussion back on the table which to me suggests the league is just focusing at the moment on continuing to grow fan numbers, continuing to grow interest, finding new fans and players through flag football and seeing where it goes in the future.

I don't think they're committed to one path or the other and it won't hurt that we're using the Formula 1 approach now and then pivot to something else later.

I tell you one thing, the commitment has never been greater among NFL owners and commissioner Roger Goodell to grow the game internationally.

It is one of the biggest things the NFL will be working on now and for many years to come and for us as fans of the game internationally that can only be good news for us.

Sports.title: 24th season in F1! Alonso extends Aston Martin deal for 2027
Sports.content:
Fernando Alonso will race on in Formula 1 with Aston Martin into the 2027 season after extending his contract with the team.

The 45-year-old will continue to race alongside team-mate Lance Stroll, whose own extended deal has also been confirmed.

Alonso, the two-time world champion from 2005-2006, will prolong his career into a record-extending 24th campaign since first racing in the sport as a 19-year-old in 2001. He has raced in 440 grands prix, winning 32, and turns 46 next July.

Aston Martin have endured a torrid first year under F1's new technical regulations in 2026, their first as Honda's works engine partners and with an Adrian Newey-led car design, scoring just three points in 15 races so far.

But the veteran Alonso, who has also been heavily critical of the sport's current engine rules, says he wants to continue on as he feels both fast enough and is "committed for the long term with this team and to helping us succeed".

"I'm very happy to sign a new contract with the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team," said Alonso, who joined them from Alpine in 2023.

An extended stay for Alonso at Aston Martin for at least an additional year had looked likely since some of the grid's other potentially-available race-winning drivers, such as Williams' Carlos Sainz, recommitted to their existing teams over the summer break.

Aston Martin's confirmation of an unchanged line-up leaves just four seats left unfilled on next year's hitherto-static grid - at Racing Bulls and Haas.

Racing Bulls are yet to confirm either of their drivers although it appears Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad are favourite to stay on.

Haas look certain to retain Oliver Bearman but Esteban Ocon's future appears likely to lie elsewhere, with F2 title leader Rafael Camara, who is backed by Ferrari, considered the front-running alternative to the experienced Frenchman.

Sports.title: How Verstappen can disrupt Antonelli, Russell title fight
Sports.content:
The 2026 Formula 1 title race has become a two-horse race between Mercedes duo Kimi Antonelli and George Russell with eight rounds remaining.

Antonelli leads Russell by 66 points ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and it will be fascinating to see how the Italian responds following what he called his "worst weekend" of the season last time out in Baku.

Depending on the quality of Mercedes' major upgrade package that will be introduced in Malaysia this week, we could see the Silver Arrows dominate the last third of the season.

However, there's one driver everyone on the grid mentions every weekend when it comes to who could challenge, or who will be a threat - and that's Max Verstappen.

This year is the first season Verstappen has not challenged for the title since 2020, having won four championships in a row from 2021 to 2024 and coming just two points short of an incredible comeback in 2025 to defeat Lando Norris.

After a difficult start to 2026, Red Bull appear to be on an upward trajectory again and history shows Verstappen will be an issue for other title protagonists.

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Malaysia This weekend Las Vegas November 20-22 Singapore* October 9-11 Qatar November 27-29 USA October 23-25 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1 *denotes Sprint weekend December 4-6 Brazil November 6-8

A repeat of 2016?

Ten years ago, Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton were duking it out for the title and Rosberg just came out on top.

It was an incredible, tense ending to the season but during the run-in, despite Mercedes having a dominant car, a 19-year-old Verstappen gave Rosberg and Hamilton a headache on a few occasions.

"My god, having him around in the races! The risk of a DNF for myself, it increases like 10-fold," Rosberg told Sky Sports F1 when reflecting on 2016.

"On my way to the championship, I had him around me every race in the last four races. He passed me I think in three of those four races, in a tussle."

Image: Nico Rosberg, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton on the podium at the 2016 Japanese GP (AP)

At the Japanese Grand Prix, Verstappen found himself ahead of Hamilton in the closing stages and was prepared to defend aggressively in their fight for second to the frustration of the British driver.

Hamilton claimed Verstappen "moved under braking" which led to the FIA clamping down on such a manoeuvre which became known as the "Verstappen Rule".

While Brazil 2016 is remembered for Verstappen's superb comeback drive in torrential rain to the podium, he was actually running in second earlier in the race after dancing around the outside of Rosberg in Turn 3.

We are yet to have a wet race or qualifying in 2026 and, in theory, the cars with most downforce should be the best in the wet. But Verstappen's ability in the rain cannot be underestimated and he will be willing to take risks when the Mercedes drivers may not, similarly to Rosberg in 2016.

Image: Max Verstappen holding up Nico Rosberg at the 2016 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix (Photo by Red Bull Content Pool/Clive Mason/Getty Images)

And in the season finale, Verstappen spun on the opening lap and dropped to the back but ran an alternative strategy and, in the middle of the race, had Rosberg behind him, who was on fresher tyres after pitting and needed to overtake the Red Bull driver.

"Tony [Ross, Rosberg's race engineer] saying it's critical we pass Verstappen for the championship…holy moly, seriously!" explained Rosberg.

"The feelings that I had in the battle and right after when I realised that I passed him, I've never had that in a race car before ever in my life."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Check out some of the best title deciders from the past decade

Are Red Bull now a genuine threat to Mercedes?

Mercedes have consistently had a quick car at every race in 2026, not always the fastest, but good enough to at least fight for the win.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull on the other hand have been up and down - all three having clear weaknesses which makes them uncompetitive at certain tracks.

On average, Red Bull have had the fourth fastest car but Verstappen impressively has the most podiums (seven) of the non-Mercedes drivers and five of those have come in the last six rounds.

Red Bull brought their last big upgrade package of the season to Baku and both drivers were happy with the new parts, which included a new floor body, diffuser and sidepods.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Verstappen was less than two tenths from snatching victory away from Russell while Isack Hadjar finished an impressive third in his first race since the end of July - it marked the first time in over two years two Red Bull drivers have featured on the podium.

"On paper, Baku was the most favourable [track] in terms of car characteristics," said Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies.

"Equally, I think the performance we've shown in the race is giving us decent hope that we will get another couple of occasions before the end of the year.

"On top of getting a couple of other occasions to get that first win, it's also good to go on tracks where it's going to be more difficult, because it's exactly what we need to be confronted with to continue to progress."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Red Bull drivers Isack Hadjar and Max Verstappen reflect on the Azerbaijan GP

The big test of Red Bull's upgrades will come this weekend at the Sepang International Circuit - a more traditional track with big medium to high-speed corners that tests a car's aerodynamics.

Tyre wear has been an issue for Red Bull but if their Baku upgrades have fixed that, Verstappen and Hadjar should be competitive again.

Verstappen: If opportunity to win is there, we go for it

This is a milestone Mekies alluded to earlier as Red Bull and Verstappen have won a race every year since 2016.

Verstappen will play things down about wanting to keep his streak of winning in 10 consecutive seasons (the record is 15 held by Hamilton and Michael Schumacher) alive, but surely deep down he is very keen to stand on the top step of the podium at least once this year.

"If Mercedes is bringing an upgrade and it works, then they take a step ahead, and that's not what you want. It will make it even more difficult to win," said Verstappen.

"But we'll try every single weekend and, of course, if the opportunity is there, we go for it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell describes his tense showdown with Max Verstappen for the Azerbaijan GP win

Depending on how Mercedes' upgrades perform and how the Red Bull fares on more traditional circuits over the remainder of the season, it is hard to say which will be Verstappen's best chance of winning.

Las Vegas in November is very similar to Baku with low tyre degradation and long straights, while Mexico City in October will be interesting due to its high altitude and which power units perform best at 2000m above sea level. In the previous regulations, the Honda power unit was very strong at altitude.

Even if Verstappen is unable to win, he will be feisty on opening laps and Safety Car restarts, knowing he has nothing to lose against the Mercedes drivers.

Although Antonelli and Russell do not need to beat Verstappen, they must be wary when fighting the Dutchman because, as he reminded us in Baku, is unrelenting and never makes your life easy on the track.

Sports.title: Woodhouse calls for fans to get behind 'one-of-a-kind' Littler
Sports.content:
Luke Woodhouse called on fans to get behind Luke Littler and "appreciate" his talents, after the 19-year-old has been subjected to boos by crowds at recent events.

Littler set out to defend his World Grand Prix title on Monday in Leicester, but was knocked out by Woodhouse in the first round, suffering a 2-1 defeat.

The world No 1 was seemingly not at his best during the match, averaging 82.41, with Woodhouse coming back from a set down to book a last-16 tie against Nathan Aspinall.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Woodhouse urged fans to get behind Littler following his victory at the World Grand Prix on Monday

Reflecting on his victory, Woodhouse urged fans to get behind Littler, hailing him for how he has elevated the sport.

"Luke's not a robot. He is going to have days and weeks where he's not right on it," Woodhouse said.

"People have echoed it and I'm going to say it again: He's a one-of-a-kind, Luke Littler.

"I hope people will take the time to appreciate how good he is and not give him a hard time and I mean really sit behind him.

"You might not see another Luke Littler ever again."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mark Webster and Michael Bridge discuss concerns over crowd whistling at the World Series of Darts

Earlier in September, Littler was subjected to boos and whistles by some areas of the crowd during the World Series of Darts Finals in the Netherlands.

Littler was booed by fans during his opening match against Danny Noppert, before again being jeered during his round-of-16 match against Aspinall. In that match, referee Charlie Corstorphine was forced to intervene to settle the crowd.

The 19-year-old had also threatened to boycott events in the Netherlands, before later pulling out of two Players Championship events in the country. He was ultimately knocked out of the tournament in the quarter-finals by Jonny Clayton.

Asked why he thinks some have been giving the back-to-back PDC World Darts Championship winner a hard time, Woodhouse said: "I don't know.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler was booed by the crowd in Amsterdam during his World Series of Darts win against Danny Noppert (Credit @OFFICIALPDC)

"He's done for the game what Phil [Taylor], Michael van Gerwen, Raymond van Barneveld and Gary Anderson have done and has taken it to the next level.

"I just hope people get behind him, give him the support and appreciate what a top talent he is.

"OK, he wasn't on it tonight and last week he lost. But he's going to win so much more stuff."

'It's a mix of emotions'

Image: Woodhouse also said 'Littler will go down as one of the sport's greats'

On Monday night, Woodhouse bounced back from losing the first set to level the match, before getting off to a flying start in the third set.

He took the first two legs, before Littler hit back in the third. From there, Woodhouse would claim the final leg to win the deciding set 3-1, and wrapped up the match with a checkout of 75.

"It's very difficult to sum up; a mix of emotions," Woodhouse said on the victory.

"I thought I threw it away in the first set, well not threw away, but I had chances to take the first set to a deciding leg and when I didn't, I was so angry with myself.

"I felt he [Littler] wasn't flying on all gears, so, I thought: 'Please don't go out and lose two sets when he's not playing well. So, it's a relief.

"I'm over the moon to beat someone like Luke on a main stage."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler took to social media to congratulate Woodhouse on his victory

Woodhouse added that sealing victory over the world No 1 was a huge achievement, but he added he was still hungry to win titles.

"Yeah, it's fantastic," Woodhouse said.

"Luke is going to go down as one of the greats, if not already.

"I'm not naive to the fact that it's a very short format; you've got to get out of the blocks quickly, double in, double out too, so I'm not naive to that.

"It's up there, but winning tournaments is what I'm here for."

Sports.title: Djokovic 'feeling good' ahead of China Open return, after US Open exit
Sports.content:
Novak Djokovic says his body is "feeling good" ahead of his return to the court at this week's China Open, following his first-round exit at the US Open.

The Serbian's bid for a record-breaking 25th Grand Slam was brought to a shock end at Flushing Meadows four weeks ago, after Djokovic was beaten over five sets by world No 45 Mariano Navone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic was knocked out in the first round of the US Open by world No 45 Mariano Navone

Djokovic battled through physical problems on a humid day in New York, with the 39-year-old vomiting multiple times during the match.

The defeat was the first time Djokovic had suffered an opening-round match loss at a Grand Slam since the Australian Open in 2006.

The former world No 1 returns this week to what has been a happy hunting ground over the years at the China Open, a tournament he has won six times.

"Yeah, feeling good so far," Djokovic said.

"Let's see. Obviously, it's completely different when you're playing ​an official match compared to practice sets or practice sessions. But so far so good.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic struggled with physical issues during his first round match against Navonne

"I was looking forward to coming to China, as I always have. My record speaks for itself on Chinese soil.

"Knowing that, it ‌also brings this dimension of confidence that I really need. Overall, it's been really good so far with the body, the way I'm feeling and playing."

Djokovic has not competed at the event since claiming his last title in Beijing in 2015.

He will face Portuguese world No 49 Nuno Borges in the opening round and could be on course to face Alexander Zverev in the quarter-finals if both players progress.

US Open champion Zverev, meanwhile, will face Britain's Cameron Norrie in the opening round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gigi Salmon joined Tim Henman and Ryan Harrison to discuss Novak Djokovic's future

Djokovic's defeat by Navone in New York saw the former world No 1 drop out of the ATP Tour's top 10 for the first time in eight years.

He is also in danger of missing out on the ATP Finals, having slipped out of the top eight qualifying spots in the Race to Turin standings and down to 15th.

The China Open will be the Serbian's eighth event of the year, with the 39-year-old still searching for his first ATP Tour title of the season.

Sports.title: How important is a fast start for teams chasing the Premier League title?
Sports.content:
The first international window gives us time to take stock and make sense of what has happened in the early weeks of the Premier League season. Manchester City are the only team to have won all five of their matches. They have started life after Pep Guardiola in the best way possible on the pitch, opening a three-point gap over champions Arsenal, but how important is a fast start?

Of course, we do not yet know the punishment they may face for breaking the Premier League’s financial fair play rules so, for the purposes of this article, we will put that matter to the side.

Enzo Maresca’s side became the 15th different team to win their opening five games of a Premier League season, and it’s the fourth occasion City have managed it. They have only won the title in one of the three previous seasons, though. They won the league in 2023-24, but failed to capitalise on their five early wins in 2015-16 and 2016-17.

That follows a wider trend across the league. Only four of the 14 teams that have won their first five matches of the season have gone on to win the title (29%): Manchester City in 2023-24, Liverpool in 2019-20, and Chelsea in 2009-10 and 2005-06.

Perhaps most importantly, all four teams went on to add to their winning streak to start those seasons. Chelsea in 2009-10 and Manchester City in 2023-24 extended their run by another game (six wins); Liverpool started with eight wins in 2019-20; and Chelsea (nine wins in 2005-06) went on the longest winning run to start a Premier League season.

Tottenham hold the record for the most consecutive wins to start a top-flight league season. They won their first 11 games in 1960-61 and, unsurprisingly, won the title that campaign. But a winning start does not guarantee success, as Manchester United found in 1985-86. Despite winning their first 10 games that season (and remaining unbeaten in their first 15) under Ron Atkinson, they collapsed and ended the season in fourth place.

It must be said, City have benefited from having an easy run of fixtures. According to the Opta Power Rankings, City had the second-easiest start this season, with their opponents having an average rating of 91.2. Only Liverpool (91.1) were handed a simpler start to the season by the Premier League fixture computer.

Another statistic that will give City fans reason for pause is that none of the previous seven clubs to start a Premier League season with exactly five wins have gone on to win the title in that campaign.

The most recent of those was Liverpool last season. The reigning champions won games against Bournemouth, Newcastle, Arsenal, Burnley and Everton to open the 2025-26 campaign before losing four in a row. The fact Liverpool won four of their first five games with goals scored after the 83rd minute pointed to their run being unsustainable, and so it proved.

Question marks about City’s defensive qualities this season suggest this may be another unsustainable winning run. Their credentials will be tested when the Premier League returns and they visit Anfield to face Liverpool, who are still unbeaten under new boss Andoni Iraola.

View image in fullscreen Illustration: Opta

The lowest position a team has finished after winning their first five games of a season is sixth (Newcastle United in 1994-95), although that did come in a 42-game campaign. Looking back at all English top-flight history, City’s current streak is the 40th different occasion of a team winning their first five games in a season. Just 14 of the previous 39 have gone on to win the league title (36%).

The average points won by Premier League champions from the first five games across the previous 34 Premier League campaigns is 11.3, which is above the total secured by Arsenal last season. They won 10 points from their first five games, dropping points by losing at Liverpool and drawing against Manchester City at home. Mikel Arteta’s side have started this season better this time around, winning 12 points from a possible 15, with their only blemish the shock 3-0 loss at Brighton.

The fewest points eventual Premier League champions have won from their first five games was in the inaugural season in 1992-93. Manchester United won only seven points from their first five matches (two wins, one draw and two defeats), but Alex Ferguson’s side recovered and finished 10 points clear of runners up Aston Villa after the 42-game season.

No team has won a Premier League title in a 38-game season after winning fewer than eight points from their first five matches. United have won the league four times after winning exactly eight points from their opening five games (in 1998-99, 2002-03, 2007-08 and 2008-09), with City replicating that feat in 2020-21. What we’re trying to say is, Hull City and Newcastle fans, it’s still possible.

The most astonishing turnaround by title winners has to be Sunderland’s effort in 1912-13, though. They failed to win any of their first seven games, drawing two and losing the other five, but they went on to win the First Division title. With just two points for a win back then, it was easier for teams to recover from a run of poor results; a monumental comeback nevertheless.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Chloe Kelly and Ella Toone dropped by England after not hitting ‘expected’ level
Sports.content:
Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly have been dropped from England’s squad because of their performance levels by Sarina Wiegman, who has given a first call-up to the 20-year-old Chelsea midfielder Lexi Potter.

Toone and Kelly have played key roles in England’s run of three consecutive major tournament finals but Wiegman made clear on Tuesday, when announcing her selection for the Women’s World Cup qualifying playoff against Greece, that she wants to see more from them for their clubs.

“The main reason is that I think the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch,” Wiegman said. The head coach said she “still believes in them” but continued: “We expect a bit more and we know they can bring more. That was the message. There is also competition going on. It’s about talent, it’s about playing minutes and it’s about the competition going on. I hope they can step up and show what they can do.

Quick Guide England squad Show Goalkeepers: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea), Khiara Keating (Liverpool), Anna Moorhouse (Manchester City on loan from Orlando Pride) Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea), Jess Carter (Gotham), Niamh Charles (Manchester City), Grace Fisk (Liverpool), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City), Maya Le Tissier (Manchester United), Esme Morgan (Washington Spirit), Leah Williamson (Arsenal) Midfielders: Laura Blindkilde Brown (Manchester City), Lucia Kendall (Aston Villa), Erica Meg Parkinson (North Carolina Courage), Lexi Potter (Chelsea), Georgia Stanway (Arsenal), Keira Walsh (Chelsea) Forwards: Freya Godfrey (London City Lionesses), Lauren Hemp (Manchester City), Lauren James (Chelsea), Beth Mead (Manchester City), Jess Park (Manchester United), Alessia Russo (Arsenal) Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I’m convinced they can do better, I think they are convinced about that too. I think they took the feedback in a good and in a positive way but it’s hard to take at the same time of course; it’s not a nice message. I hope they respond to it really well. We will support them and of course they get the support at club too. I hope they come back even better than they were before.”

Neither Toone nor Kelly has scored or provided an assist in the WSL this term, although Toone did score in Manchester United’s 10-1 League Cup win over second-tier Sheffield United last week, after she had been left out of their draw at Arsenal. Toone has started three of United’s four WSL games. Kelly has started one of Arsenal’s league games and their Champions League victory over Køge and made three WSL substitute appearances.

There was also no place for the Chelsea forward Aggie Beever-Jones. Wiegman has called up the uncapped 18-year-old midfielder Erica Meg Parkinson and the London City Lionesses winger Freya Godfrey, and there is a return after injury for the captain, Leah Williamson.

There had been growing calls for the inclusion of Potter this term after her strong form for Chelsea, including her starring role in Sunday’s 1-0 victory over Arsenal. “She’s grown a lot,” Wiegman said. “Last season we kept a close eye on her because she was getting into the squad and playing really well. But I think she’s started the season so well. Her performances have really impressed us so she really deserves this call-up.

“She’s shown at Chelsea that she can start against any team. The last game I thought she did very well against a top Arsenal [team]. What I’ve seen from her is that she comes out on the pitch and no matter who she plays against, she’s just going to play and she’s comfortable. I hope to see that next week.”

The Lionesses face Greece in the first leg at the Pankritio Stadium in Heraklion, Crete, on Friday 9 October before the return at Leicester’s King Power Stadium the following Tuesday, needing victory to reach December’s second, decisive round of the playoffs.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

England are having to contest the playoffs despite winning five of their six matches in their qualifying group, having missed out on top spot to the world champions, Spain, based on the head-to-head record from their meetings in April and June, in repeats of the 2023 World Cup final. England will be heavily fancied to progress to next summer’s finals in Brazil.

That tournament could be Wiegman’s last with England because her contract expires after the World Cup. She gave little away when asked about any contract discussions, saying: “We have regular conversations together, and we talk about the future at moments, but at this point I’m just focusing on Greece. We want to get through and qualify for the World Cup. Of course I talk to Mark [Bullingham], every two weeks, and we speak about what’s happening now, what’s in the future, but there’s nothing new now.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino ready to accept demands for larger payouts from $6bn reserves
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, is poised to bow to demands from Uefa and Concacaf to distribute more money from its $6bn cash reserves to member associations.

In a letter sent on Monday to all six confederation presidents and copied to members of the Fifa council, Infantino indicated his willingness to “support the greatest level of additional funding”, without committing to the $10m-per-member that has been proposed.

Infantino was responding to a joint letter sent by the Uefa and Concacaf presidents, Aleksander Ceferin and Victor Montagliani, earlier this month, who called for an additional payout for all of Fifa’s 211 members of at least $10m during the 2027-2030 commercial cycle, a demand which was subsequently endorsed in a separate letter from the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa.

Infantino said the presidents’ proposals will be considered by the Fifa council during its next meeting on 15 October, after the secretary general, Mattias Grafström, has consolidated the suggestions. Under the proposed terms of Infantino’s abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, the member associations would have received an additional $20m during the next four-year cycle, plus a further payment of $20m had they signed up before a 53-day deadline that would have expired last week.

“I will not prejudge the amount,” Infantino wrote in the letter. “I will support the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered through Fifa’s proper governance process, applied fairly and supported by transparent and auditable arrangements. The ambition is welcome. The financial evidence, governance and implementation must now support it.

“A single figure can begin the discussion, but it cannot complete a global policy. I have therefore instructed the Secretary General to consolidate all submissions into one integrated assessment for consideration by the Fifa council on 15 October 2026.”

Infantino also used the letter to mount another defence of his role in FFE, which he claimed was an attempt to increase Fifa’s investment in football. “The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable Fifa to invest more in football – not to replace support that could responsibly be provided from existing resources,” he wrote.
