World.title: Matric exams 2026: Why THESE past papers could be your secret weapon
World.content:
With South Africa’s 2026 matric exams fast approaching, Grade 12 learners are entering the crucial final stretch of their preparation. Image: Inside Education

With South Africa’s 2026 matric exams fast approaching, Grade 12 learners are entering the crucial final stretch of their preparation.

The National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations are scheduled to begin next month, with the official Department of Basic Education (DBE) timetable showing the first examinations taking place from Tuesday, 13 October and run until Thursday, 26 November.

For learners who are still working through their revision, there is one resource that should not be overlooked: past examination papers.



DIARISE | Matric exams: Important dates every Grade 12 learner should know

Why past papers matter

The DBE itself recommends using previous examination papers to prepare for the upcoming NSC exams, saying they can help learners identify what they already know and where they need more revision.

Past papers provide learners with an opportunity to move beyond simply reading notes and textbooks.

By actually answering questions under exam conditions, learners can practice applying what they have learnt – an important difference when preparing for a three-hour examination.

1. Get used to the exam format

Past papers can help learners become familiar with the structure of their subjects.

This includes the types of questions asked, how marks are allocated and how much work may be required within the available examination time.



Knowing what to expect can also make the actual examination environment feel less unfamiliar.

2. Identify your weak areas

One of the biggest benefits of working through old papers is that mistakes become obvious.

A learner may feel confident about a particular section of the syllabus until they encounter a question requiring them to apply that knowledge.

Marking the paper afterwards can highlight topics that need additional attention.

3. Practice managing time

Time management is particularly important during the NSC examinations.

Learners can use past papers to practise completing a full paper within the official time limit.

Instead of stopping after every difficult question, they can learn when to move on and return to a question later.

4. Learn from the memorandum

Past papers become even more useful when learners work through the corresponding memorandum after completing the paper.

The goal should not simply be to see whether an answer is right or wrong.

Learners should look at how marks are awarded and compare the required response with their own answer.

This can be particularly useful for subjects where showing calculations, explaining concepts or providing specific points is important.

5. Build confidence through practice

Revision can become overwhelming when learners try to cover an entire year’s work at once.

Working through past papers provides a more structured approach.

A learner can complete one paper, identify problem areas, revise those topics and then return to another paper to see whether their performance has improved.

Where to find matric past papers

The DBE provides previous NSC examination papers and memoranda on its official website.

The department’s past-paper resource currently includes papers from several years, including the 2026 May/June examinations, 2025 November examinations and earlier NSC examinations.

The 2026 May/June NSC/SC papers are also available by subject.

If you are writing your matric exams next month, study hard and good luck!

What time do matric exams start?

The DBE timetable has two standard examination sessions.

Morning papers begin at 09:00, while afternoon papers start at 14:00.

Week 1: 13 to 17 October

The first week opens with CAT and IT practicals, followed by language papers. English Paper 3 – the writing and composition paper – falls on Thursday 15 October, which is earlier than many students expect.

World.title: Herman Mashaba says Moonshot Pact cost ActionSA votes
World.content:
ActionSA leader, Hwrman Mashaba, at the IEC ROC in Midrand during the 2024 elections. Image: Nokwanda Ncwane

ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba says the party’s association with the Democratic Alliance (DA) through the Moonshot Pact contributed to its decline in support.

Mashaba made the remarks during an interview with the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC) on Tuesday, ahead of the 4 November Local Government Elections.

ActionSA received 2.48% of the vote in the 2021 local government elections. Its support fell to 1.20% in the 2024 national and provincial elections.



HERMAN MASHABA SAYS MOONSHOT PACT COST ACTIONSA VOTES

During the interview, Mashaba said he had previously warned that ActionSA would face consequences for its association with the DA through the Moonshot Pact.

“We got punished. The black voters said they will not vote for ActionSA because if we give our votes to ActionSA, they’re going to give our votes to the DA. So, we got punished for that and that is why we’re making it very, very clear. I want South Africans to know that ActionSA is a completely independent political organisation,” he said.

The Moonshot Pact was formed by several opposition parties ahead of the 2024 national elections, with the parties seeking to provide an alternative to the African National Congress (ANC). ActionSA was among the parties involved.



Despite his criticism of the previous arrangement, Mashaba said ActionSA remained open to working with other political parties, including the DA.

“We are willing to work with anyone, including the DA, as long as they can deal with the Helen Zille issue,” Mashaba said, referring to DA Johannesburg mayoral candidate Helen Zille.

LGE 2026 | Herman Mashaba says ActionSA's ties to the DA cost the party votes, but says future coalition is possible if the "Helen Zille issue" is resolved. pic.twitter.com/vJw6jAP3nr  September 29, 2026

ACTIONSA LEADER ALSO IN THE RACE FOR JOBURG MAYORAL CHAIN

Herman Mashaba is ActionSA’s mayoral candidate for Johannesburg in the upcoming local government elections.

He previously served as Johannesburg mayor from 2016 to 2019 while representing the DA before resigning from the party.

ActionSA is among the parties contesting the City of Johannesburg, where 80 parties are registered to contest proportional representation seats in the 2026 local government elections, according to the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC).



Several political parties have already announced their candidates as they prepare for what is expected to be a highly competitive Johannesburg mayoral race.

The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) has selected Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng as its mayoral candidate while the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) has also entered the Johannesburg mayoral race for the first time, selecting Mlungisi Mabaso as its candidate.

Other parties contesting the mayoral race include Rise Mzansi, which has named Lukhona Mnguni; Build One South Africa (BOSA), which has selected Nobuntu Hlazo-Webster; the Land Party, which has selected Ntsiki Mazwai; and Al Jama-ah, which has named Shireen Ebrahim.

World.title: Aston Martin keep Lance Stroll for 2027 – and no one knows why
World.content:
Confirmed: Fernando Alonso will drive alongside Lance Stroll at Aston Martin for the 2027 Formula One season. Image: X @AstonMartinF1

Former world champion Fernando Alonso has quashed retirement talk after confirming he will stay with Aston Martin for the 2027 Formula One season.

Alonso had been considering ending his illustrious racing career, but his passion for driving convinced him to remain at the British-based team for at least one more year.

The 45-year-old Spaniard, who won successive world titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, will drive alongside Aston Martin team-mate Lance Stroll for a fifth consecutive season.



READ | Business heavyweights look to bring Formula One back to South Africa

‘Committed for the long term’

“I took my time to make this decision, but racing is my life, my passion, and I know I still have the speed and determination to compete at the highest level,” Alonso said in a team press release on Tuesday.

“I’m committed for the long term with this team and to helping us succeed. I truly believe in what we are building: we have strong leadership, incredible people, partners and facilities.”

All-time great

Alonso is regarded as one of the sport’s all-time greats, with 32 race wins and 106 podium finishes.

Despite the arrival of technical guru Adrian Newey, Aston Martin have struggled this season and sit 10th in the constructors’ championship with just three points from the first 15 rounds.

Canadian Stroll is set to enter his 11th Formula One season in 2027, having first signed with the team in 2019.



Shocking season

Stroll has been shockingly poor this season, having finished just four of the 15 races to date, scoring zero points to date.

Alonso has faired slightly better, picking up the team’s only three points thanks to a 10th-place finish in Monaco and a ninth-place finish at the Dutch Grand Prix.

He has finished nine of 15 races to date.

Aston Martin are 10th out of the 11 teams this season, only ahead of point-less Cadillac.

World.title: School calendar: When does Term 4 end?
World.content:
With Term three officially being over, South African pupils are entering the home stretch of the 2026 academic year. Here’s everything you need to know about the final term.

WHEN DOES TERM FOUR END?

According to the Department of Basic Education’s official 2026 school calendar, Term 4 begins on Tuesday, 6 October and runs until Wednesday, 9 December 2026. Administration days follow on 10 and 11 December, officially closing out school for 2026.

Term 4 spans 10 weeks, making it one of the shorter terms of the year. However, it does match Term 3 in length. In total, it covers roughly 47 school days (or 49, including the administration days at the end).



Unlike earlier terms, which included breaks for holidays like Freedom Day, Workers’ Day, Youth Day and National Women’s Day, Term 4 has no public holidays falling within it. That means it will run as a continuous, uninterrupted stretch of learning right through to December, giving teachers a solid run to complete the curriculum before the year wraps up. Take a look at how many public holidays are left for 2026 here.

Once schools close on 9 December, the 2026 academic year officially ends. Learners then head into the long December school holiday, which overlaps with public holidays including the Day of Reconciliation and Christmas.

A FULL RECAP OF THE 2026 SCHOOL YEAR

Term 1: 14 January – 27 March (11 weeks)

14 January – 27 March (11 weeks) Term 2: 8 April – 26 June (12 weeks)

8 April – 26 June (12 weeks) Term 3: 21 July – 23 September (10 weeks)

21 July – 23 September (10 weeks) Term 4: 6 October – 9 December (10 weeks)

6 October – 9 December (10 weeks)

These dates applied to the public schools under the Department of Basic Education. Independent and IEB schools often set their own calendars. So, if your child attends a private school, it’s worth double-checking directly with them, as dates can differ slightly.



With Term 4 starting on 6 October and running through to 9 December, parents and pupils have a clear run to the end of the year. No public holiday breaks means it’s a term for finishing strong, so it’s worth getting back into a routine early.

World.title: Bankrupt Lawrence Dallaglio to sell 2003 Rugby World Cup winner’s medal
World.content:
Former England star Lawrence Dallaglio is selling his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner's medal after being declared bankrupt. Image: Budds

Former England star Lawrence Dallaglio is selling his 2003 Rugby World Cup winner’s medal after being declared bankrupt.

Dallaglio is auctioning off medals, trophies and caps from his glittering career following a costly divorce last year.

READ | Four Springboks whose Test futures are in serious doubt



British & Irish Lions cap up for auction

The 54-year-old shone for England during their run to glory at the World Cup 23 years ago, culminating in their 20-17 final victory against Australia in Sydney.

The World Cup medal is listed with an estimate of between £50 000 and £80 000 by auctioneer Budds, with the whole collection having an estimated value of £180 000 (R3.9 million).

Budds lists 22 items in the ‘Lawrence Dallaglio Collection’, including a 2003 Six Nations winner’s medal, other medals from his successful club career with Wasps and a British and Irish Lions cap.

Financial difficulties

Earlier this year, former England captain Dallaglio spoke about his financial difficulties during an appearance on the High Performance podcast.

“As a result of getting divorced, I was made bankrupt so I had some financial problems,” he said.

“I could have done things a lot better.”



Dallaglio said he needed therapy after his divorce and bankruptcy, which left him wallowing in “self-pity”.

The auction will take place on October 13 in Northamptonshire.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse
