World.title: All Estonian ministries saw wage hikes in the past year
World.content:
Average pay rose at every Estonian ministry over the past year, with the largest increases at the regional affairs and culture ministries. Pay grew slowest at the education and justice ministries.

The draft state budget for next year sets out changes in pay and staffing at the ministries between June 1, 2025 and May 31, 2026. Average pay rose at every ministry, with increases of more than 10 percent at two of them.

One was the Ministry of Culture, which has 91 employees. Its average pay rose 13 percent over the year to €3,713, while its workforce shrank by one.

"Base salaries had remained virtually unchanged for the previous couple of years, weakening the ministry's position on pay and increasing turnover, particularly among experienced experts," the explanatory memorandum to the budget said.

Meanwhile, the average gross salary of cultural workers was €2,090 last year and is projected to reach €2,263 this year. The minimum salary for cultural workers with higher education is €1,720 and will remain at that level next year.

Average pay at the Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture rose 14 percent over the year to €3,635. Its workforce fell by 36 to 250.

At the Ministry of Defense, average pay rose 9 percent to €3,922. The number of employees increased by eight to 149.

Average pay rose 7 percent at both the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of the Interior. At the latter, it stood at €3,639 at the beginning of June, while the number of employees fell by three to 166. Average pay at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs rose to €3,675.

Pay rose 6 percent at both the Ministry of Climate and the Ministry of Economic Affairs. Their average pay was also nearly identical: €3,706 at the Ministry of Climate, which has 266 employees, and €3,703 at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, which has 160.

The Ministry of Finance recorded a 5 percent rise in average pay. Its workforce fell by three to 243 and average pay stood at €3,472.

Pay at the Ministry of Social Affairs rose 4 percent. Its workforce grew by four to 173.

At the bottom of the pay growth table were the Ministry of Education and Research and the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs, where average pay rose 3 percent each.

The Ministry of Education and Research's workforce fell by 10 to 260 and average pay rose to €3,320. At the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs, average pay was €3,660 and the workforce fell by 40 to 224.

According to Statistics Estonia, the average salary in Estonia was €2,243 in the second quarter of this year, up 5.5 percent from the same period last year.

World.title: Isamaa head: The state budget one of continued chaos
World.content:
Opposition Isamaa leader Urmas Reinsalu called the coalition's 2027 budget a continuation of chaos. He said the next government must revise is to cut public sector spending.

"This is a manipulation carried out on paper to create the impression that the state's finances are improving. They are actually getting worse. The documents build in delayed spending and unrealistic revenue expectations," Reinsalu said in a speech after the budget was submitted.

He argued that the government was merely postponing spending and would leave a mess behind for the elections.

"The Reform Party boasts that it has now reduced debt. In reality, the debt burden is growing at an accelerating pace: general government debt is set to rise by 1.9 percent of GDP in 2026, 2.5 percent in 2027 and 4 percent in 2028. Interest costs alone will climb from €272 million in 2026 to €635 million by 2030."

The Isamaa leader called several items included in or omitted from the state budget and the state budget strategy bluffs on paper.

As examples, he cited what he described as an inflated estimate of the maximum potential revenue from renting out prison space and a sharp projected increase in corporate income tax revenue. Meanwhile, he said, the €150 million cost of an explosives plant had been excluded from the budget strategy's balance calculations.

"The shifting of spending between years is a sleight of hand in its own right. Through a supplementary budget for 2026, the government wants to bring forward some spending from 2027 and change the rules for accounting for the purchase of stockpiles. The aim of all this is to make the 2027 budget look healthier."

Reinsalu also claimed that the policy of raising taxes would continue, with increases in fuel and energy excise duties planned in the budget. He objected to what he called the budget's continuing lack of transparency.

"This is illustrated by the billions in previously unspent budget funds and a quarter of a billion euros sitting in SmartCap's account."

The Isamaa leader said a new, expenditure-based budget framework law should be adopted (after Riigikogu elections — ed.) in spring 2027, along with a supplementary budget that cuts spending and reduces government operating costs.

"We must make a real contribution to improving the finances of families with children and reduce the burden of indirect taxes. We must give economic growth a genuine boost."

Isamaa is leading all polls ahead of the 2027 Riigikogu elections.

World.title: Supreme Court: Publishing expunged conviction details partly unconstitutional
World.content:
Estonia's Supreme Court has ruled that indefinitely publishing certain expunged drug and arson convictions is unconstitutional, meaning the Riigikogu will have to revisit the legislation.

The Criminal Records Database Act lists offenses for which the names and personal identification codes of convicted people remain publicly available in court rulings online even after their criminal records have been expunged.

As of June 9 this year, the provision affected 8,714 people, including 5,362 convicted of handling a large quantity of drugs, defined as at least 10 doses.

Five people convicted of crimes between 2006 and 2017 asked the court to stop publishing their information. Four had been convicted of drug offenses and one of arson.

The applicants argued that publishing information about expunged convictions harmed their reputations and those of their family members and made it harder for them to support themselves and find work. The Tartu Circuit Court found their requests justified and initiated a constitutional review of the provision.

In two rulings published Tuesday, the Supreme Court emphasized that the constitution allows interference with a person's private life to protect public order and the rights and freedoms of others. "Publishing information about expunged convictions serves the legitimate aim of preventing new serious crimes and protecting other people's fundamental rights," the court said. But it found that indefinitely publishing the information of everyone convicted of a drug offense or arson was neither proportionate nor justified.

The Supreme Court agreed with the circuit court that the drug offenses covered by Section 184 of the Penal Code can vary greatly in severity, depending, for example, on the substance and quantity involved and whether it was supplied to others. Sentences also range widely, from one year to life in prison. In these cases, the applicants received suspended prison sentences close to the minimum and a long time had passed since the offenses, the court noted.

For arson under Section 404, the law provides for a fine or up to five years in prison, meaning the legislature has not classified it as a serious crime. The provision punishes conduct that endangers a person's life or health, even if no actual harm results. It also does not distinguish an isolated act of arson from a pattern of behavior, including pyromania. In this case, the applicant committed the offense in 2006 at age 18 and has not since been convicted of a similar crime.

The Supreme Court said that publishing information about expunged convictions effectively amounts to an additional lifelong social punishment. "It makes it difficult for a person who has served their sentence to reintegrate into society, limiting their opportunities in their private life, work and education. Stigmatizing information may also affect the convicted person's loved ones, including minor children," the court said in a statement.

The Supreme Court therefore declared the Criminal Records Database Act unconstitutional and invalid insofar as it requires information about a person convicted of a drug offense under Section 184(1) or (2) of the Penal Code or arson under Section 404 to remain public in a court ruling after the conviction has been expunged from the criminal records database.

Several ways the Riigikogu can amend the law

The Supreme Court's ruling took effect immediately for the five applicants and for others convicted of the same offenses whose requests to remove their information are currently before the courts. For everyone else with expunged convictions for those offenses, the court delayed the ruling's entry into force by six months to give the Riigikogu time to amend the law.

The Supreme Court explained that publishing information about expunged convictions may still be justified in some drug and arson cases and that lawmakers have several ways to address the issue. For example, they could allow courts to assess whether publication is necessary in each case when a convicted person requests the removal of their information. They could also link publication more broadly to the length of the sentence, whether it was served in prison or other factors indicating the seriousness of the crime or the danger posed by the offender.

The Supreme Court said lawmakers should also avoid creating unnecessary additional work for the courts. Any solution must comply with European Union law.

World.title: Iraq becomes South Korea’s sixth-largest oil supplier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Official data indicates that Iraq was the sixth-largest supplier of crude oil to South Korea in August 2026, with a volume exceeding 3.8 million barrels.

South Korea’s total crude oil imports stood at 91.33 million barrels in August 2026, marking a 2.2 percent decline compared to the 93.35 million barrels recorded in August 2025 and a two percent drop from the 93.18 million barrels imported in July 2026.

South Korea’s oil imports from Iraq stood at 3.82 million barrels in August 2026, over a 65 percent decrease compared to the 11.105 million barrels imported during the same month in 2025, with no Iraqi imports reported in July.

The input text is clear and maintains a consistent tone. However, it could benefit from a slight restructuring for improved flow. Here’s a revised version:

Saudi Arabia was the largest exporter of oil to South Korea, supplying 21.66 million barrels. The United States followed with 17.92 million barrels, while the UAE ranked third with 16.76 million barrels. Kuwait provided 7.58 million barrels, and Oman contributed four million barrels.

The figures mark a decline in the share of Iraqi oil in the South Korean market compared to the previous year, with import volumes from Iraq dropping by approximately 7.27 million barrels.

Iraq was the fourth-largest crude oil supplier to South Korea in the first half of 2026, accounting for 7.4 percent of the country’s total oil imports.

According to the Korea Petroleum Association (KPA) and the Korea National Oil Corporation, South Korea imported 467.12 million barrels of crude oil in the first half of the year, an eight percent decline compared to the same period in 2025.

The value of the country’s oil imports increased by 8.1 percent to $41.36 billion as global oil prices surged. Iraq’s average oil shipments to South Korea totaled 113.7 million barrels in 2025, which is an average of 311,500 barrels per day.

World.title: Alonso to stay with F1 team Aston Martin in 2027
World.content:
London – Former world champion Fernando Alonso has quashed retirement talk after confirming he will stay with Aston Martin for the 2027 Formula One season.

Alonso had been considering ending his illustrious racing career, but his passion for driving convinced him to remain at the British-based team for at least one more year.

The 45-year-old Spaniard, who won successive world titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006, will drive alongside Aston Martin team-mate Lance Stroll for a fifth consecutive season.

“I took my time to make this decision, but racing is my life, my passion, and I know I still have the speed and determination to compete at the highest level,” Alonso said in a team press release on Tuesday.

“I’m committed for the long term with this team and to helping us succeed. I truly believe in what we are building: we have strong leadership, incredible people, partners and facilities.”

Alonso is regarded as one of the sport’s all-time greats, with 32 race wins and 106 podium finishes.

Despite the arrival of technical guru Adrian Newey, Aston Martin have struggled this season and sit 10th in the constructors’ championship with just three points from the first 15 rounds.

Canadian Stroll is set to enter his 11th Formula One season in 2027, having first signed with the team in 2019.

World.title: NATO, EU allies rally to Estonia after ‘sabotage’ blamed on Russia
World.content:
Tallinn – EU and NATO leaders on Tuesday rallied in support of Estonia and Ukraine after Tallinn accused Russia of “sabotage” in an August arson attack on a drone manufacturer, a claim the Kremlin immediately rejected.

“Russia continues its reckless campaign of hostile actions against NATO allies. It is trying to weaken our resolve and stop our support for Ukraine,” NATO chief Mark Rutte said.

He added: “But Russia is failing. It is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine and it is failing to undermine our unity and support for Ukraine.”

Estonia’s foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, said an investigation into the August 15 arson attack against the defence company Milrem Robotics, which makes ground drones used in Ukraine, determined that Moscow was responsible.

“We can conclude with certainty that the arson attack… was an act of sabotage ordered by the special services of the Russian Federation,” he said on X.

He said the perpetrators had been arrested, and Russia’s ambassador had been summoned.

Tsahkna said that “this act of sabotage is part of Russia’s broader campaign across Europe, aimed at intimidating us and weakening our support for Ukraine”.

– Kremlin denial –

The Kremlin swiftly dismissed Estonia’s accusation as “baseless” and with “absolutely no relation to reality”.

“We cannot and will not take such statements seriously,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow in response to an AFP question.

Estonia has repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid provocations since the beginning of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Along with its neighbours, Latvia and Lithuania, the country has ramped up defence investment and remains a staunch ally of Kyiv.

The European Union said it stood with Estonia calling the arson attack “reckless”, and would not be put off supporting Ukraine.

“Moscow is trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine. This will not happen,” European Commission spokesman Christian Wigand said.

French President Emmanuel Macron also called the arson attack a “dangerous escalation” by Russia, and another in a “multiplication of these hostile acts”.

“Russia needs to know that it will not overcome our unity or our determination to continue supporting Ukraine,” Macron said on X.

“Russia’s fingerprints are all over” the Estonia attack, Lithuanian foreign minister Kestutis Budrys wrote on X, adding that Moscow’s “hostile activities do not stop at Ukraine’s borders”.

Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics added that “more support for Ukraine … will be needed and must be provided”.

Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson called the attribution of the attack “extremely serious” and “directed against Europe as a whole”.

World.title: US grants waiver for Iranian flights at Najaf Airport
World.content:
Najaf (IraqiNews.com) – An informed Iraqi government source revealed on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, the operational circumstances behind the U.S. administration’s acceptance of an exemption request submitted by Baghdad regarding restrictions on Iranian commercial aviation at Najaf International Airport.

Speaking to Shafaq News Agency, the source explained that while major commercial airports across Iraq rely on international ground-handling contractors bound by U.S. Department of the Treasury directives prohibiting U.S. dollar transactions with Iranian air carriers, Najaf International Airport operates under a distinct administrative model staffed entirely by Iraqi personnel, enabling logistical fee settlements in alternative currencies such as the euro, Iraqi dinar, or Iranian toman.

Administratively detached from the federal Ministry of Transport, Najaf International Airport operates as an autonomous operational directorate under the local government of Najaf Governorate. The facility had continued rendering ground handling, baggage, and refueling services to Iranian airlines until a U.S. Treasury enforcement notice led the Governor of Najaf to issue an administrative directive halting services to avoid exposing the airport to secondary sanctions.

However, following formal representations directed by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi—who tasked the Minister of Foreign Affairs with negotiating a targeted waiver with U.S. officials—a pathway was cleared allowing the Council of Ministers or the local governorate administration to issue an executive order authorizing the resumption of ground services without triggering international penal measures.

Despite the breakthrough in waiver negotiations, conflicting reports persist on the tarmac regarding immediate flight resumption. While national carrier Iraqi Airways issued a brief statement announcing the restart of scheduled flights to Iranian destinations via Najaf, high-level airport authorities and federal aviation officials confirmed later Tuesday that ground operations for Iranian airlines remain technically paused pending formal ministerial ratification.

Because global ground-handling contractors operating across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra airports remain barred from processing dollar-denominated aviation fees under U.S. secondary sanctions, Najaf’s sovereign operational structure positions it as Iraq’s primary transit gateway capable of handling bilateral pilgrim traffic and regional commercial flights through non-dollar financial settlements.

World.title: Iraq faces Saudi Arabia in decisive Gulf Cup 27 Group A finale in Jeddah
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi national football team faces host nation Saudi Arabia on Tuesday evening, September 29, 2026, in a decisive Matchday 3 encounter to settle the final standings of Group A at the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup.

Kicking off at 8:30 PM local time on the pitch of the King Abdullah Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, the regional derby will determine which side claims the top qualifying spot heading into the tournament’s semifinal bracket.

Tournament hosts Saudi Arabia enter the fixture atop Group A with a flawless record of 6 points, having secured back-to-back victories while scoring four goals and maintaining consecutive clean sheets. Iraq sits in second place with 4 points, earned from an opening victory and a hard-fought draw, netting four goals while conceding three.

While the Green Falcons have already sealed mathematical qualification to the knockout stages, the Lions of Mesopotamia require a positive result—a win or a draw—to guarantee second-round passage and eliminate any threat from third-placed Oman, who square off simultaneously against Kuwait.

To oversee the high-profile fixture, the tournament’s organizing committee appointed Dutch FIFA referee Danny Makkelie to lead the officiating crew.

With Saudi Arabia targeting a maximum 9-point haul to close the group stage and Iraq aiming to leapfrog into first place with a victory, the encounter represents one of the most anticipated matchups of the competition, pitting two of the region’s most decorated footballing programs against each other before an expected sellout crowd in Jeddah.

World.title: US dollar climbs back to 158,000 IQD range across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar rebounded across Iraq’s parallel currency exchanges on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, snapping a four-day downward trajectory and climbing back toward the 158,000-dinar threshold in Baghdad, with regional bourses in Erbil and Basra recording corresponding price gains.

The upward adjustment reverses the brief dip into the 156,000–157,000 dinar range recorded late last week, re-expanding the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 to over 20 percent.

Market tracking published by the 964 Network showed that major exchange desks in Baghdad quoted cash selling rates at 158,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 157,000 dinars, registering a 1,000-dinar climb compared to midweek levels. In Erbil, the commercial hub of the Kurdistan Region, parallel bureaus quoted selling figures at 157,800 dinars per $100, with buying rates closing at 156,500 dinars.

In the southern trade center of Basra, trading mirrored the regional upswing, where retail counters offered greenbacks at 157,500 dinars for sale while maintaining buy orders at 156,500 dinars.

The renewed upward pressure across currency trading floors comes as domestic wholesale merchants and private importers step up cash procurement ahead of end-of-month commercial settlements, absorbing market supply despite recent government announcements regarding incoming dollar cash shipments.

Currency brokers note that while bilateral understandings reached during high-level meetings in New York have bolstered long-term liquidity expectations, day-to-day parallel desks continue to respond rapidly to immediate corporate cash demand and physical banknote availability in Baghdad’s primary wholesale bourses.

World.title: FIFA accuses UEFA of ‘misinformation campaign’ in bid for World Cup papers
World.content:
Paris – FIFA has accused European football’s governing body UEFA of a “misinformation campaign” in its bid to access documents related to Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell off parts of the World Cup.

In FIFA’s response in a court case in Florida, it says that UEFA’s attempt to force the world body to hand over the documents is designed to “influence” the FIFA presidential election scheduled for next year.

In the 26-page legal filing, FIFA says UEFA is acting “for purposes of harassment, rather than out of any legitimate need for discovery” in pursuing its case against world football’s governing body.

It accuses UEFA of acting “in bad faith”.

FIFA president Infantino caused uproar in July with proposals to create a commercial subsidiary to run its biggest events, such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

The plan would have allowed private investors to acquire stakes in a company created under the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. The backlash that followed led to the proposals being quickly shelved.

FIFA says in its court filing that UEFA makes “numerous false or misleading statements” about Infantino and the world governing body, including that he “sought to profit personally from the FFE proposal”.

FIFA’s court filing says that UEFA’s application “fails on both the facts and the law”, and should therefore be denied.

UEFA said it had no comment to make when contacted by AFP.

– FIFA’s vast reserves –

UEFA has filed a request in Florida for permission to gather evidence for a potential criminal complaint in Switzerland, where both UEFA and FIFA are based.

European football’s governing body said last month that alongside “other interested parties” it was “preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement”.

UEFA, the federation that represents World Cup holders Spain and football powerhouses such as France, England and Germany, is leading the opposition to Infantino, calling openly for his removal.

FIFA confirmed this month that Infantino will stand again for president in the election next March, despite the backlash over his now-abandoned private investment plan.

Infantino sent a letter to FIFA’s 211 members this week indicating that a greater amount of money could be distributed to FIFA members from its vast cash reserves.

Earlier this month, UEFA urged FIFA to make $10 million available to each of its member associations — a total of $2.1 billion — “for investment in infrastructure and football development”.

In the letter seen by AFP, Infantino said he would support “the greatest level of additional funding that can responsibly be delivered”.

Infantino insisted in the letter that the abandoned proposal to sell off World Cup commercial rights had been intended to generate additional money for football.

“The recent commercial proposal, now withdrawn, was intended to enable FIFA to invest more in football,” Infantino wrote.

FIFA has an estimated $6 billion of unused cash reserves and UEFA argued that Infantino did not need to try to raise capital given how much money his organisation was already holding onto.

Infantino is not without friends — 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body CAF and South America’s CONMEBOL also supportive.

South American nations including Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay will host a match during the next World Cup in 2030. The tournament will be mainly held in Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

World.title: US studies exempting flights from Iran to Iraq’s Najaf from sanctions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US administration is studying granting a limited waiver from Iran’s sanctions program to allow aircraft transporting Shia Muslims to and from Iraq for religious pilgrimages.

According to Reuters, the US Treasury Department permission would allow Iraqi Airways to operate flights to and from the Iraqi city of Najaf for one month, with the potential of extending the waiver later.

On September 25, Najaf International Airport announced the suspension of all flights arriving from and departing to Iran.

The airport administration suspended all flights arriving from and departing to Iran, effective from 02:00 on Friday, September 25, 2026, until further notice, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The consequences of the new US sanctions on Iran’s aviation sector are developing quickly, as governments, airports, and airlines rush to reassess their relationships with Iranian carriers, fearing secondary sanctions from Washington.

The development has led to the suspension and cancellation of several international flights and disrupted Iran’s air transport network.

These measures follow a new package of US sanctions comprehensively targeting Iran’s aviation sector, including companies that provide refueling, maintenance, ground handling, and ticketing services to Iranian carriers.

Amid mounting fears about losing access to the dollar-based global financial system, several businesses have decided to suspend or reduce their activities with Iranian airlines.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the new measures aim to intensify economic pressure on Iran, noting that Iranian airlines would face increasing difficulties in operating international flights if foreign airports and service providers refused to deal with them.

World.title: Cyber fraud can outwit the tech-savvy too, IIT study finds
World.content:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: A career in IT and security did not save her from losing Rs 90 lakh to cybercrime. The professional, with 28 years of experience, was among 33 victims interviewed for an IIT Madras-led study that found technological familiarity could be overwhelmed by fear, urgency and psychological manipulation.Participants came from Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, New Delhi and Mumbai; the sample included 12 senior citizens. Participants included bankers, doctors, IT professionals and people with cybersecurity certifications. One reported a loss of Rs 1.12 crore even after recovering Rs 25 lakh.Published in Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, the qualitative study explores how victims were deceived, rather than measuring national risk. Its urban, professionally employed sample cannot establish that educated people are more vulnerable than others.Many participants were navigating illness in the family, retirement, job searches or workplace pressure. Fraudsters exploited these circumstances through investment promises, employment offers or threats to reputation. Some victims sought quick returns; others paid because they feared arrest or harm to relatives.âThe way they act and talk, you cannot believe that they are not police officersâthey play a psychological game with you,â the IT and security professional said in the study.In âdigital arrestâ scams, victims described being confined to rooms, monitored over video and coached to mislead bank managers. A plastic surgeon said: âThey emotionally manipulated and trapped me: every half an hour I had to send them pics that I am aloneâ.In task-based scams, criminals initially paid victims for simple online assignments to build trust, then pressed them to invest larger sums and borrow from relatives or friends when funds dwindled.The researchers also found neglected device updates and missing security software among participants. Their accounts suggest psychological manipulation can work alongside technical weaknesses. Some victims subsequently abandoned online payments and returned to cash.The damage extended beyond bank balances. Victims reported sleeplessness, shame and strained family relationships. Institutional responses were uneven: some banks helped, while others blamed customers; some victims reported being sent between police stations.The researchers call for awareness campaigns explaining specific fraud tactics, stronger police expertise, faster bank detection and better coordination between banks, police and courts. âThe response to cybercrime must move beyond blaming victims,â said IIT Madras adjunct faculty member P Kandaswamy in a statement.

World.title: New NCERT book says Indian kings received swords from goddesses to resist religion-driven invasions
World.content:
NCERTâs new class nine social science textbook, released on Tuesday, mentions that many kings and princes received swords from goddesses such as Kali, Durga, and Bhavani to resist invasions since the seventh century.

The chapter titled "Resistance and Resilience" in the book "Understanding Society India and Beyond-Part 2" outlines successive invasions of the Indian subcontinent since the seventh century.

"Annamaraja, ruler of Bastar is believed to have received his sword from Manikyadevi (Danteshvari) while Kumara Kampana (Vijayanagara) was believed to have used a goddess-given sword against the Sultanate forces at Madurai.

Similarly, Shivaji is also traditionally believed to have obtained a sword from goddess Tulja Bhavani," the chapter reads.

The chapter also describes religious traditions in warfare, with the worship of goddesses being a long-standing tradition.

World.title: Power crisis part of bid to privatise power sector: Pinarayi Vijayan
World.content:
The power crisis in the State is part of a covert political move to hand over the power sector to private players, Keralam’s Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said. Speaking after inaugurating a seminar on ‘Privatisation Policies of the Central-State Governments and the Power Crisis’, organised by the Kerala chapter of the Electricity Employees Federation of India, he said the country’s total power generation capacity was almost double of its peak demand.

At the same time, private monopolies control 60% of the country’s power generation, and the crises are being engineered to enable private firms to reap exorbitant profits, he alleged. In Keralam, despite receiving sufficient indications of the crisis as early as the first week of June, the government deliberately dragged its feet on the issue, he said.

The politics behind the crisis is no different in the State, where the crises are often engineered -- particularly during UDF tenures -- to undermine the credibility of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), after which the private sector is presented as a saviour, he alleged. The government is now looking to favour the corporates seeking to gain control of the power sector, Mr. Vijayan said.

However, the State government should understand that privatisation cannot be implemented easily in Keralam, where strong resistance was mounted during the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government’s tenure, he said. The blame game over the power crisis by the Chief Minister and other Ministers was part of an attempt to mask their own incompetence and interests, he alleged.

Failed to adhere to norms

The Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission (KSERC) cancelled the long-term power purchase agreement because the UDF government led by Oommen Chandy had failed to adhere to established norms, and the responsibility for the current crisis lay entirely with the UDF, Mr. Vijayan said.

On the one hand, construction of the battery energy storage project is progressing slowly, while on the other, moves are underway to pave the way for corporates such as the Adani Group to gain a foothold in the sector, he alleged.

The UDF Minister has also spoken of establishing a nuclear power plant, a move that is linked to the NDA government’s legislation opening up the nuclear energy sector to private players. The recently passed SHANTI Act would pave the way for private players to enter the nuclear sector, he alleged. He also pointed out that the privatisation agenda initiated by the UPA government was now being aggressively pursued by the BJP-led government at the Centre. Former Power Minister A.K. Balan presided over the function.

World.title: CCB searches 5 locations in private school approval fraud case
World.content:
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) of the Greater Chennai Police on Tuesday carried out searches at five locations, including houses of the aides of former Minister Anbil Mahesh Poyyamozhi, in the private school approval fraud case.

The CCB is investigating the case, which was registered based on a complaint alleging that money was collected from private school managements by promising to obtain government recognition and various statutory approvals for them.

On September 16, the CCB personnel searched the houses and offices belonging to Mr. Mahesh Poyyamozhi and his aides Valadi Karthik, Arun Prakash, and Prakash in Chennai and Tiruchi. Documents and electronic devices were seized during the searches and are being examined as part of the investigation.

The police also conducted searches at the houses and shops in Kallakurichi, which belong to Saravanan, Ramesh, and Gokulakrishnan, relatives of Muthukumar, who allegedly assisted in cheating private school managements and collecting money from them. More than 30 documents were seized during those searches.

Continuing the investigation, the CCB personnel on Tuesday conducted searches at five houses in Saligramam, Kodambakkam, Choolaimedu, Poonamallee, and Navalur in Chennai. The premises belonged to B.T. Arasakumar, another relative of Muthukumar and the aides of Mr. Mahesh Poyyamozhi.

The police seized 44 documents related to the case and one laptop during the searches. Further investigation is under way.
