World.title: ‘Strategic procedural pause’: Impeachment court suspends September 30 trial
World.content:
Senator-judges listen to a manifestation by prosecution counsel Gerville Luistro during Day 30 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 28, 2026.

Impeachment court Reginald Tongol explains the suspension was due to the trial being 'aggressively ahead of schedule'

MANILA, Philippines– The Senate impeachment court has suspended the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte slated for Wednesday, September 30.

The Senate Clerk of Court announced this in a notice dated September 29, and also said that the trial will resume on Thursday, October 1, at 10 am.

Impeachment court spokesperson Reginald Tongol said the postponement was not due to delays, but because the trial was “aggressively ahead of schedule.”

“Tomorrow is a deliberate Strategic Procedural Pause designed to clear the floor so both panels can prepare for the grueling, whole-day marathon sessions running continuously from October 1 to 15,” Tongol said in a press statement.

“This pause gives all parties the critical breathing room needed to digest the highly technical, voluminous financial records incoming from the Anti-Money Laundering Council and the Registers of Deeds starting this Thursday,” he said.

Former Senator Antonio Trillanes IV is also expected to be presented as prosecution witness on October 1, the first implementation of the whole-day trial. – Rappler.com

World.title: Should Baste Duterte get a free pass for ‘missing’ VP Sara’s ties to Gencorp?
World.content:
Davao City Mayor Sebastian 'Baste' Duterte takes the witness stand on Day 31 of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on September 29, 2026.

Senator-judge Bong Go defends the Davao City mayor's decision to delegate signing powers, saying the younger Duterte is not the one on trial

While some grilled Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte over his decision to delegate procurement responsibilities — his defense for supposedly not knowing anything about the his city govenment’s deals with Gencorp Industries Inc. — other senator-judges came in his defense, citing the sheer volume of work mayors handle.

Duterte took the witness stand on Tuesday, September 29, for the impeachment trial of his older sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

In his testimony, the mayor distanced himself from the Davao City government’s deals with Gencorp, maintaining he had no direct hand in the contracts sealed with the company linked to the Vice President.

The younger Duterte claimed he did not personally review Gencorp’s contracts and did not personally approve such deals because he did not interfere in the undertakings of city hall’s bids and awards committee. He also said he delegated his procurement responsibilities to Davao City Assistant City Administrator Tristan Domingo because of his workload as mayor.

Senator-judge Christopher Lawrence “Bong” Go, in a rare manifestation, defended this decision, citing the voluminous documents the Davao City mayor needed to review and sign.

Play Video

“Mayor Baste Duterte is not the one on trial here,” said Go.

“I am a witness to the work in the city hall. Davao City is a huge city, and a mayor has a lot of documents to sign. It is impossible for him to go over each document, so he really needed to delegate the task,” he said. Go had served as aide to Duterte’s father, former president Rodrigo Duterte, for four of his seven terms as Davao City mayor.

Senator-judges Alan Peter Cayetano and Joel Villanueva expressed similar remarks, noting the younger Duterte may have to sign at least 2,500 to 3,000 documents a week.

“The point I want to make is this: You will not have any other time to govern if you’re going to have to look at each and every company, each and every document, each and every person…. Under the law, you can rely on the signature of your personnel officer,” Cayetano said.

Senator-judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, for his part, asked the mayor if he was advised on the Arias doctrine, as it contained a similar legal principle.

“I asked if you were advised on the Arias doctrine because it lays out the rule that heads of offices are permitted to rely, on good faith, on their subordinates for their action, processing, recommendations,” Lacson said.

Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo urged Mayor Duterte to investigate the city staff and administrator who allowed the contracts between Gencorp and the city government.

Mayor Duterte, however, dismissed Tulfo’s manifestation, saying, “as long as my sister’s name, the Vice President’s name, was not on the contract, then there’s nothing.”

Outside the courtroom, the prosecution spokespersons said they found the mayor’s insistence that he knew nothing about the Gencorp deals, and that these were aboveboard, difficult to believe.

Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV also offered a contrasting view, warning of the implications of allowing mayors to rely entirely on delegated authority when transactions involve their relatives.

Trillanes, who attended the trial in case he would be called as a prosecution witness on the explained wealth case against the Vice President, was initially hesitant to respond to reporters’ questions in a chance interview during a break in the trial.

When pressed to comment on Mayor Baste’s appearance at the trial, Trillanes finally said: “Siguro heto lang. I’ll give you this. Kung puwede ‘yung sinasabi niya, lahat ng mayor sa Pilipinas puwedeng makipagkontrata sa kapatid nila. They will just feign ignorance. So think about that. ‘Yun ang implication dito.“

(Okay, it’s like this. I’ll give you this. If what he says is allowed, all the mayors in the Philippines can sign contracts with their siblings. They will just feign ignorance. So think about that. That’s the implication here.)

Play Video

– Rappler.com

World.title: Unmatched EJ Obiena shatters Asian Games record to defend throne
World.content:
CHAMPION. Pole vaulter EJ Obiena in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.

EJ Obiena delivers the Philippines' third gold medal in the 2026 Asian Games as he breaks his own record to repeat as men's pole vault champion

MANILA, Philippines – When it comes to Asia, EJ Obiena is in a league of his own.

And he reinforced that notion as Obiena defended his Asian Games crown following a record-breaking performance in men’s pole vault at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.

Obiena set a new Asian Games mark after clearing 5.91 meters in a single attempt, delivering the Philippines’ third gold medal in this edition after gymnastics star Carlos Yulo won the first two in artistic gymnastics.

He shattered his own record of 5.90m, which Obiena set in 2023 when he won his first Asian Games title in Hangzhou, China.

After two failed attempts at 5.80m, Obiena upped the ante by going for 5.91m, which he surpassed with room to spare on the way to becoming the first back-to-back champion in the event since Kazakhstan’s Igor Potapovich won in 1994 and 1998.

It marked the second time in the last two months Obiena cleared over 5.90m after failing to do so in two years – a proof of his improved shape as he slowly but surely rediscovers his old form.

Two Chinese bets completed the podium, with Yao Jie and Li Chenyang bagging silver and bronze, respectively, with 5.70m clearances.

Obiena highlighted the Philippines’ best athletics showing in decades, with the country also bagging a pair of bronze courtesy of John Cabang Tolentino (men’s 110m hurdles) and Victoria Bossong (women’s 800m). – Rappler.com

World.title: COA finds ‘unverifiable’ beneficiaries in DepEd’s SHS voucher program
World.content:
The dozens of unverifiable beneficiaries of the senior high school voucher program resulted in an overpayment of P938,000, according to state auditors

MANILA, Philippines – There were 58 “unverifiable” beneficiaries of the Department of Education‘s (DepEd) senior high school (SHS) voucher program, which resulted in an overpayment of P938,000 in school year (SY) 2025-2026, the Commission on Audit (COA) found.

According to COA’s compliance audit on the existence and eligibility of voucher beneficiaries, the flagged unvalidated beneficiaries were:

32 students who had officially or unofficially dropped out

12 who transferred to other schools

11 who were not enrolled in the second semester

2 who were reported deceased

1 who was absent during validation with no records available

The overpayment of P938,000, which was for 53 out of the 58 unverified beneficiaries, had already been released to their respective schools, COA said in its 2025 annual audit report on the DepEd released last September 23.

Four beneficiaries were excluded from billing statements prior to payment as of February, while the subsidy for one beneficiary had not yet been released as of March.

Moreover, state auditors found five beneficiaries who were “misclassified under incorrect voucher categories,” resulting in an overpayment of P14,710.

Other deficiencies seen were incomplete or improperly maintained supporting documents and inadequate monitoring by the DepEd and the Private Education Assistance Committee, which helps in implementing the Government Assistance to Students and Teachers in Private Education (GATSPE).

“These lapses expose the program to the risk of erroneous billing and overpayment, compromise the reliability of beneficiary validation, and may result in the disbursement of funds to ineligible beneficiaries, contrary to the objective of providing financial assistance exclusively to qualified learners,” COA said.

The SHS voucher program is a government financial subsidy program for qualified Grades 11 and 12 students. It provides assistance in the form of vouchers ranging from P14,000 to P22,500 per year, which are paid directly to the student’s chosen private school.

COA said the program’s participating schools are responsible for encoding and updating student information.

“The status of the concerned [voucher program beneficiaries] should have been duly updated and subjected to DepEd verification to prevent potential overpayments,” the commission added.

On Tuesday, September 29, the DepEd said it had acted on the COA findings.

“As part of its five-layer validation, DepEd, through its co-manager of the senior high school voucher program, Private Education Assistance Committee, has completed its school year 2025-2026 validation. Through this year-end validation, flagged cases are being reviewed and confirmed overpayments will be recovered,” part of the DepEd’s statement read.

The agency said it had “tightened beneficiary validation, billing, refund, and accountability measures” in the revised Expanded GATSPE guidelines released in April.

The DepEd said it will “continue to pursue accountability and the recovery of government funds where warranted.”

Issue of ‘ghost students’

The DepEd investigated 12 private schools in February 2025 over the alleged presence of ghost students in the SHS voucher program.

By March 2025, the agency recovered P65 million from the voucher program amid irregularities, with 38 private schools fully refunding the government.

In July 2026, the DepEd said a regional trial court had sentenced an individual to up to 14 years in prison for attempting to defraud the government program by submitting falsified documents. Case details were not provided.

In the same 2025 annual audit report, COA also flagged deficiencies in monitoring the implementation of the SHS voucher program.

As of October 2025, there were 172,909 billed beneficiaries in participating private senior high schools nationwide, excluding the Bangsamoro region and the Negros Island Region, according to COA.

State auditors found the unverifiable beneficiaries from a sample population of 5,507 in SY 2025-2026. Of the number, 995 beneficiaries came from the National Capital Region, while the rest were from other regions, covering 571 senior high schools participating in the voucher program. – Rappler.com

World.title: Victoria Bossong claims 800m bronze in Asian Games debut
World.content:
REPRESENT. Athletics standout Victoria Bossong in action for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games.

The fastest in the heats, Victoria Bossong finishes third in the women's 800 final as she delivers the Philippines' second athletics medal in the 2026 Asian Games

MANILA, Philippines – Victoria Bossong turned in a slower time in the final but still salvaged an athletics medal for the Philippines in the 2026 Asian Games as she snagged the bronze in the women’s 800m at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan on Tuesday, September 29.

The Filipina-American middle-distance specialist clocked 2 minutes and 5.34 seconds to finish third and deliver the Philippines’ second athletics medal in this edition of the quadrennial showpiece after John Cabang Tolentino bagged bronze in the men’s 110m hurdles.

China’s Wu Hongjiao struck gold with 2:04.49, while Bahrain’s Nelly Korir clinched silver with 2:05.16 — the three medalists separated only by less than a second.

Bossong, whose mother, Catalina Atienza, hails from Oriental Mindoro, emerged as the title favorite after posting the fastest time in the heats, where she registered 2:02.34.

A repeat of that time would have netted the 23-year-old Harvard University graduate the Philippines’ first Asian Games gold medal in a track event since the late Lydia de Vega ruled the women’s 100m in the 1986 edition.

But it simply was not meant to be for Bossong, who owns a personal best of 1:58.52 — a time that eclipses the Asian Games record of 1:59.02 set by Kazakhstan’s Margarita Mukasheva in 2014.

Still, Bossong enjoyed a promising debut for the Philippines in a multi-sport event, which came just months after she gained eligibility in July to represent the country. – Rappler.com

World.title: Jaime T. Cruz: The business partner of Sara, Baste, and Pulong Duterte
World.content:
Businessman Jaime T. Cruz also had close ties with former president Rodrigo Duterte, who once offered him the post of PhilHealth president and CEO

MANILA, Philippines – Jaime T. Cruz is not just a business partner of Vice President Sara Duterte.

Cruz also has business ties to the Vice President’s brothers, Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte.

Testifying before the impeachment court on Tuesday, September 29, Baste confirmed that he knows Cruz and that they are business partners.

Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) records presented during the trial show that Cruz is president of Chinese Gen Bee Food Corporation, where Baste and Pulong are members of the board.

Play Video

Cruz is also a business partner of Sara in Metro City Chow Foods Corporation, and an incorporator of several other companies that Sara declared as business interests in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs).

Rappler’s investigation also found that Cruz is among the shareholders linked to Gencorp Industries Inc., a company declared in Sara’s SALNs. The investigation revealed that Gencorp secured contracts from Davao City Hall while Baste is the mayor.

Ties to ex-president Duterte

Cruz’s ties to the Duterte family also extend to their father, former president Rodrigo Duterte.

On October 15, 2019, then-president Duterte appointed Cruz as special envoy to China for trade and investments. Months before that, Duterte had offered Cruz the position of Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) president and CEO. Duterte eventually appointed Ricardo Morales to lead the state health insurer.

Play Video

Cruz and Gencorp president Kimberly Cruz were part of the business delegation that accompanied Duterte to his working visit to Japan in May 2019. It was during this trip when the two, representing Dohtonbori Philippines, secured a deal to operate Karayama outlets in the Philippines, as well as an agreement granting them development rights for the Dohtonbori Okonomiyaki restaurant businesss in the country. – Rappler.com

World.title: How often have barangay, SK elections been postponed?
World.content:
Rappler crunches the numbers and finds that both elections have been moved — either separately or jointly — at least 16 times since 1982

The barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections (BSKE) supposed to be held this year have been officially moved to November 2028 after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed a law fixing these officials’ terms to five years.

This is now the third time Marcos has authorized a BSKE postponement. But the current president is not the only one to have moved the polls — nor is it rare for such a delay to happen multiple times in one administration.

“Barangay and SK elections are already the most frequently postponed democratic exercises in the country’s history,” poll watchdog National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections (Namfrel) said in a September 26 statement criticizing the 2026 BSKE postponement.

So, how often have these postponements actually happened?

Rappler crunched the numbers and found that both elections have been moved — either separately or jointly — at least 16 times since 1982. Here’s a breakdown of the data.

How often terms were extended because of BSKE postponements This chart shows the start and end of an elected official’s term, starting from the election they won until the successfully held election that chose their successor. Hover over or tap data points for more details Scroll horizontally to see full timeline on small screens All Elections Status: Completed Postponed Scheduled National and local elections (NLE) Loading election data…

1988 barangay elections, postponed twice

The first-ever barangay polls were held on May 17, 1982, in accordance with the Barangay Election Act of 1982. Before that, elections for barangay officials had been held together with the local elections. (

The terms of office of these barangay officials were set to six years, which means the next election would have been on the second Monday of May 1988.

But most 1982 barangay election winners were not able to finish their terms, since local elected officials were replaced by appointed officers-in-charge following the EDSA Revolution in 1986.

The May 1988 elections were then postponed twice: first to November 1988 and then to March 1989, which was when the polls finally pushed through.

The succeeding 1994 election proceeded on schedule, but the Local Government Code had limited the terms of office of those elected in these polls to just three years.

The 1997 elections were then promptly conducted after those three years.

1992 SK elections, postponed twice

The first SK polls in 1992 also got off to a rocky start, with two postponements right off the bat.

The landmark election should have been held 30 days after the May 1992 local elections, but the Commission on Elections (Comelec) passed a resolution setting the polls on September 30, 1992.

In the end, the elections were moved again and finally conducted on December 4, 1992.

1994 SK elections

The 1991 Local Government Code set the second Monday of May as the date for the 1994 barangay officials, with the SK polls set to happen 120 days after, but only the barangay polls pushed through. An amendment to the law had been passed, resetting the SK elections to May 1996.

The same amendment set the barangay elections for May 1997, which was successfully conducted. Elected SK officials were to serve until the next regular election of barangay officials — which should have been three years later in 2000.

Change in term limits in 1998

Then-president Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo passed a law in 1998 changing the terms of barangay and SK officials from three to five years, starting with those elected in May 1997.

This meant the next barangay and SK polls would be in 2002 instead of 2000. Another amendment to the Local Government Code would later set the exact date of the synchronized BSKE on July 15, 2002, which was successfully held.

2005 BSKE

The next synchronized polls were then postponed once again from 2005 to 2007, which a 2005 Philippine Star report said was prompted by the Arroyo administration saying there was no money available for the polls.

At the time, P6.4 billion had been allocated for a charter change plan, the same report said. This plan did not come to fruition.

The 2007 and 2010 BSKEs then proceeded as scheduled.

2013 SK election

The 2013 polls only pushed through at the barangay level. The SK elections were once again postponed, although there was no holdover for then-incumbent youth officials, who stepped down from office at the end of their terms on November 30, 2013.

The new date for the SK polls was set between October 28, 2014, and February 23, 2015. This did not go as planned, either.

2015 SK elections, postponed twice

The 2015 SK polls were first set for February 21. But as the election date drew near, another bill seeking the SK polls’ postponement to October 2016 had passed in both houses of Congress, awaiting only the president’s signature.

Because of this, the Commission on Elections initially moved the polls to April 2015.

A month before the April polls, then-president Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III signed the law moving the SK polls to October 2016.

2016 BSKE

Then-president Rodrigo Duterte signed another law postponing the BSKE schedule by one year, from October 2016 to October 2017.

At that point, barangay officials were set to go beyond their three-year terms, since the new law also allowed a holdover for them to continue serving unless removed or suspended from office.

SK posts, meanwhile, had been vacant since 2013.

2017 BSKE

Duterte authorized another postponement of the BSKE — just three weeks before the scheduled polls — and set it for May 2018.

The 2018 BSKE finally pushed through on May 14, 2018. It replaced the barangay officials who had been serving for nearly two years beyond their allotted terms, and filled the SK seats that had been vacant for four and a half years.

2020 BSKE

Duterte again moved the BSKE originally set for May 2020 to the first Monday of December 2022. This gave elected officials a term of five years — beyond the three-year limit required by law.

2022 BSKE

The 2022 BSKE was again postponed by Duterte’s successor, Marcos. It was moved to October 2023 and successfully conducted.

2025 BSKE

The succeeding elections were supposed to be conducted on December 1, 2025, but were again postponed after Marcos signed a law increasing the term of barangay officials from three to four years.

The next elections were scheduled for the first Monday of November 2026.

2026 BSKE

Marcos granted another term lengthening for barangay and SK officials from four to five years, effectively postponing the polls to November 2028.

Who postponed the most BSKEs?

Barangay and SK election postponements Number of times elections were postponed during each administration Barangay only SK only Both

Postponements have mostly been evenly distributed across presidencies — although each had its own context.

Noynoy Aquino’s postponements were only composed of SK polls, during a time when the Sangguniang Kabataan Reform Act of 2015 was being created in response to criticisms of the barangay youth arm being inefficient and corrupt. (READ: Why the Sangguniang Kabataan needs an overhaul)

In Ramos’ case, two of the three postponements were only months apart.

It is during the last two administrations that postponements became regular for both the barangay and SK polls — and usually spanning one year or more.

Why are these postponements so frequent? Ona Caritos, executive director of election watchdog Legal Network for Truthful Elections, said that the delays are a “carrot” dangled by national and local officials to gain the support of barangay leaders.

“They [can] say, ‘Oh, I’m the one who filed the term-setting bill,’ or ‘I’m the one who filed this postponement of the elections yet again,’” she explained.

And while national and local officials get their incentives, voters get the short end of the stick when underperforming leaders overstay their welcome.

“We can file cases against them, but that’s not an opportunity or an avenue that all of us could explore. So, elections are the most basic accountability measure that every one of us could exact accountability from our elected officials,” Caritos said.

The law to postpone the 2026 BSKE may have been signed by the President, but the onus to set the record straight on these postponements lies with the Supreme Court.

While the Supreme Court had already declared unconstitutional postponing elections without a compelling reason, it has not yet ruled on changing term limits that result in election delays. Now, a petition against the term-setting law has already been filed, with more possibly on the way.

For Caritos, these petitions are the only measures left against the 2026 BSKE postponement. With how frequent BSKEs have been postponed in the last three decades, the impact of the Supreme Court’s decision must go beyond this year’s polls.

“To avoid the possibility, yet again, of postponing the 2028 Barangay and SK elections… then there’s a need for the Supreme Court to really clarify what would be the decision when it comes to a situation like this,” she said. – Rappler.com

Coding for the charts used in this story was done with the assistance of AI.

World.title: Why everyone wants a piece of the Lopez group’s Energy Development Corp.
World.content:
The Lopez group, through First Gen, bought Energy Development Corp. from the government in 2007 and has spent the 19 years since learning how deep the asset actually goes

Three foreign groups have sought different stakes in the same Lopez asset: an Indonesian tycoon has made an unsolicited US$5 billion offer to buy it outright, another Indonesian conglomerate has entered a joint venture to build with its geothermal know-how, and this September, a new investor paid P25.77 billion for nearly a fifth of its parent company, First Gen Corporation, at P36 a share, just P1 above the price First Philippine Holdings (FPH) had recently rejected as inadequate.

What they are circling is Energy Development Corporation or EDC, which turns 50 this 2026 and draws electricity out of hot water and steam trapped beneath the volcanic rock of Leyte, Negros, Bicol and Mindanao, generating power around the clock whether or not the sun shines or the wind blows, without needing fuel deliveries from anywhere. (READ: The company the Lopezes gave up Meralco for: EDC, from oil crisis child to takeover target)

The Lopez group, through First Gen, bought EDC from the government in 2007 and has spent the 19 years since learning how deep the asset actually goes.

What 50 years underground buys

“We have invested more than P200 billion through the years to build approximately 1,300 megawatts (MW) of reliable baseload capacity,” Francis Giles Puno, president and chief operating officer of First Gen and of its parent First Philippine Holdings (FPH), told shareholders at the group’s annual meeting on Friday, September 25.

But money alone is not the barrier to entry. The knowledge is.

Solar and wind developers can measure much of their resource before construction begins, while geothermal developers have to drill into the earth to prove what is actually there, deciding where to sink an expensive exploration well before knowing exactly what they will find, learning how a reservoir behaves as pressure changes across decades, and figuring out how to keep mineral deposits from damaging the wells and pipes that carry geothermal fluids. Enough wrong decisions can shorten the productive life of a field.

The Lopezes understood early what they had bought. Three years after the acquisition, Federico “Piki” Lopez told First Gen shareholders in the company’s 2010 annual report that the group was “prepared to go global and take this geothermal power development expertise, built on EDC’s ’35-year head start,’ into parts of the world that have only begun to tap their existing reserves.” Puno, writing as president in the same report, described EDC as having “existing steam concessions and a great technical platform supported by its scientists and engineers.”

That 35-year head start is the same clock that reaches 50 this year.

EDC has been doing this since the 1970s, across generations of geologists, reservoir engineers and drillers who learned the craft from the people before them, but not all of that accumulated capability remains housed inside EDC today. Part of it migrated into another branch of the Lopez group through ThermaPrime Drilling Corporation, incorporated in December 2010 and, by its own account, “staffed by many of the same people who comprised the original PNOC (Philippine National Oil Company)-EDC drilling team.” It sits not under EDC or under First Gen but beside them, owned by First Balfour, the group’s construction arm, which FPH owns outright. The drilling knowledge that had accumulated inside EDC was replicated elsewhere in the group and became a business of its own.

Puno highlighted ThermaPrime in his September 25 report to FPH shareholders. “Major infrastructure and renewable energy development demand specialized capabilities built over decades,” he said. “Through First Balfour and ThermaPrime, FPH has developed the engineering, construction and drilling expertise to take on increasingly complex projects.” ThermaPrime, he said, “brings equally specialized capabilities to geothermal development. Its people and equipment helped EDC accelerate its drilling program, completing close to 30 wells over the past 3 years.”

That intensive program has now ended, and the numbers show it. Activity moderated this year, Puno said, with ThermaPrime’s revenues declining 49% to P1.4 billion and net income falling 45% to P276 million.

But the rigs have found work elsewhere. ThermaPrime completed a 4-year program for SM Investments-owned Philippine Geothermal Production Company, drilling 12 production wells and 3 multilateral injection wells. In July, Maibarara Geothermal Inc., the Yuchengco-led venture of PetroGreen Energy, ACEN, and PNOC Renewables, awarded it a 2026-2027 exploratory campaign: 3 firm wells and one contingent well in Batangas and Laguna, to depths of 2,100 to 3,000 meters, with drilling running from October through May 2027.

Puno told shareholders he expects the drilling expertise to be sold beyond the group’s own projects. “The value of these capabilities extends beyond the projects they serve today,” he said, with ThermaPrime “exploring opportunities to bring its geothermal drilling expertise to Japan, Taiwan and Indonesia.”

Puno described a business the company keeps spending on rather than harvesting. “We continue to learn invaluable lessons and reinvest significant resources to maintain, expand, and strengthen our unique leadership position in geothermal,” he said, “including the forthcoming re-envisioning and redevelopment of Leyte.”

The capability built around EDC over half a century is therefore broader than the plants and steam fields sitting on EDC’s books: it includes knowledge about where to drill, how to manage a reservoir and how to keep drawing power from it over decades, while some of the specialized drilling and well-engineering capability that grew out of the old EDC has already become a separate business elsewhere in the Lopez group.

Buy it, or build with it

The US$5 billion offer was not the first time an Indonesian group came looking.

More than a year earlier, a different Indonesian house had approached the Lopezes with a different proposition. Sinar Mas, the conglomerate controlled by the Widjaja family with interests running from palm oil to paper mills to telecommunications, did not make an offer for EDC. It signed a joint venture with it, bringing into Indonesia the geothermal capability the company had spent decades building in the Philippines.

The two sides signed an initial agreement in August 2025 and formalized the partnership in Jakarta that October, pairing PT FirstGen Geothermal Indonesia with PT DSSR Daya Mas Sakti, a unit of the Sinar Mas energy company PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa. The 50-50 joint venture targets roughly 440 megawatts across 6 fields in West Java, Flores, Jambi, West Sumatra and Central Sulawesi. By March this year, EDC said the partners were looking at spending about $30 million for the exploration phase alone and hoped to begin drilling at least one well later in 2026.

JOINT VENTURE. Officers of PT FirstGen Geothermal Indonesia, a subsidiary of Energy Development, the largest RE producer in the Philippines and part of Lopez-owned First Gen Corporation, sign a joint venture with PT DSSR Daya Mas Sakti, a subsidiary of PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk, part of Sinar Mas, on the development and management of geothermal resources with a combined potential of approximately 440 megawatts, across six strategic fields located in West Java, Flores, Jambi, West Sumatra, and Central Sulawesi, on August 27, 2025, in Jakarta, Indonesia. Courtesy of First Gen Renewables

Indonesia holds about 40% of the world’s geothermal reserves, according to EDC, or some 24 gigawatts. Yet only about a tenth of that potential has been developed.

What it does not have in the same measure is 50 years of EDC’s practice.

“We are bringing close to 50 years of geothermal experience and expertise to Indonesia,” Jerome Cainglet, EDC’s president and chief operating officer, said when the partnership was announced. “At the same time, we know that there is also a lot that we can learn there, which we may use in the Philippines.”

His counterpart was equally explicit about what the Indonesian side hoped to gain. “Our goal is to strengthen national capacity in geothermal development and to fully harness the country’s natural potential for clean energy,” said Lokita Prasetya, president-director of PT DSSR Daya Mas Sakti.

Puno described the same partnership to his own shareholders on September 25: the group is “bringing our expertise to Indonesia through opportunities jointly pursued with the Sinar Mas Group.”

Play Video

Sinar Mas is paying to use what EDC knows, while ThermaPrime sells another part of the geothermal capability developed around EDC to outside customers. Neither requires the Lopez group to sell EDC itself.

Then came July 2026, and a different Indonesian tycoon.

PT Barito Renewables Energy, controlled by Prajogo Pangestu, made an unsolicited, indicative and non-binding proposal to acquire EDC for an equity value of approximately $5 billion, subject to due diligence, transaction documents and regulatory and corporate approvals. First Gen said at the time that there had been no discussions between the parties, no agreements signed and no advisers appointed.

The offer came while the Lopez cousins were in the middle of a public fight over control of its companies, other parts of the corporate structure were confronting their own liquidity needs, and ABS-CBN was trying to raise billions in fresh capital.

There is also a limit to how simply the Lopezes can treat EDC as theirs to sell. First Gen controls EDC with 65% of the votes but has only a 45.8% economic interest, while Philippines Renewable Energy Holdings Corporation or PREHC— the consortium through which Macquarie-managed funds and Singapore’s GIC invested in EDC in 2017—owns 34.9% of its voting stock. The structure gives First Gen control despite holding less than half of EDC’s economic upside, but it leaves another large financial investor with substantial money at stake in any change of ownership.

Then on September 21, First Gen ended the takeover speculation, telling the Philippine Stock Exchange: it “confirms that there are currently no plans to divest itself of EDC, and there are no firms, other than PT Barito Renewables Tbk, looking to potentially acquire EDC.”

First Gen’s own investment plans also show where it intends to put capital next. Puno said the company could spend as much as P160 billion over the next 5 years, including around P70 billion for geothermal exploration and expansion and more than P60 billion for hydropower, with the balance going into solar and other opportunities.

More capital is going into geothermal than into the pumped-storage hydro projects the company recently bought into.

The math behind keeping EDC is visible in First Gen’s own books. In the first half of 2026, EDC generated P29.88 billion of First Gen’s P41.15 billion in consolidated revenue, representing 72.6% of the total. Having sold 60% of its natural gas business to Enrique Razon’s Prime Infrastructure, and with its Wawa and Pakil pumped-storage hydro projects not scheduled to come online until 2030 or 2031, First Gen would be left holding a portfolio whose returns arrive largely at the end of the decade. EDC is what pays the bills today. (READ: The business case of the Lopez-Razon gas and hydro deals)

It is also earning more. EDC’s net income contribution to First Gen rose 73.5% to P3.69 billion in the first 6 months of 2026, up from P2.12 billion a year earlier. First Gen attributed the increase to higher average selling prices, improved generation across its steam fields, and battery energy storage systems that began coming online from September to December 2025.

Put those pieces together and the strategic choice becomes clear: Barito wants to own EDC, Sinar Mas wants to build alongside it, and external developers can hire ThermaPrime for the most specialized parts of the drilling. The Lopez group does not have to sell EDC to monetize what 5 decades of geothermal development built.

What the new shareholder bought

The interest in the Lopez geothermal business has also extended one corporate level above EDC.

On September 10, KKR, the American private equity firm that had held a stake in First Gen for 6 years, sold its entire holding of 715.86 million shares (19.99%) to Angsana Finance Limited, a Cayman-incorporated entity owned by Gateway Holdings Limited and managed by Singapore-based Gateway Partners, at P36 a share.

That transaction followed a formal rejection on August 15, when FPH notified the stock exchange it had turned down KKR’s proposal to acquire part of FPH’s holding and launch a voluntary tender offer for First Gen’s public float at P35 a share. “After careful deliberation and consideration,” the filing read, “FPH has determined that KKR’s proposal does not represent FGEN’s true value.” Angsana paid P36 for KKR’s block less than a month later.

Asked by Rappler at the September 25 FPH stockholders’ meeting what governance rights Angsana acquired with those shares, Puno said there was none.

“Because KKR acquired its [common shares equivalent to] 19.9% stake in First Gen directly from the secondary market, no shareholder agreement was established with FPH,” Puno said. “Consequently, Angsana did not obtain any special or contractual governance rights through its purchase of KKR’s holdings, maintaining only the standard statutory rights granted to minority shareholders under the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines.”

The 19.9% is smaller than it looks. That total accounts only for First Gen’s common shares. Measured against First Gen’s total issued capital, which includes the voting preferred shares that FPH owns outright, Angsana’s stake comes to 14.06%.

Gateway has not publicly explained what it sees in First Gen or what it ultimately expects from its P25.77 billion outlay. The purchase by itself does not establish that Angsana expects any transaction involving EDC. But underneath those shares sits a portfolio that Puno says is now 92% renewable, built around what he called “hard to replicate assets”, with EDC at its center and an unsolicited offer already putting an approximately $5-billion equity value on the geothermal subsidiary.

What 50 years is worth

For most of its corporate life, EDC created value primarily by converting underground heat into megawatts for the Philippine grid.

Play Video

But 50 years later, that accumulated know-how are creating value in several ways at once: as a cash engine that First Gen wants to keep and expand, as an acquisition target commanding multibillion-dollar benchmarks from foreign suitors, as an exportable development capability in Indonesia with Sinar Mas, and through ThermaPrime, as specialized drilling and well-engineering services that can be sold across the industry.

First Gen has already shown it is willing to sell a major asset when doing so advances its strategy. In 2025, it sold 60% of the natural gas business it had spent decades pioneering to Prime Infrastructure, releasing capital as the company shifted toward a portfolio that is now overwhelmingly renewable. At the same time, it is preparing the comprehensive redevelopment of its flagship Leyte geothermal complex and continuing to pour billions into new wells.

Its public position on EDC, despite Barito’s $5-billion approach, is unequivocal: EDC, for now, is staying.

When the Lopez group bought EDC from the government 19 years ago, the debt burden during the 2008 global financial crisis was so severe that the family famously had to surrender its controlling stake in Meralco to Manuel V. Pangilinan just to protect its balance sheet.

What they preserved was more than power plants and steam fields. They acquired an ecosystem of knowledge that had been developing since the 1970s, then spent the next 19 years adding to it. Part of that capability remains embedded in EDC’s fields, engineers and reservoir expertise, part has migrated into ThermaPrime as an independent drilling arm, and part is now being deployed across Indonesia’s volcanic belts.

In 2010, Piki Lopez wrote that the group was prepared to take EDC’s expertise into parts of the world that had only begun to tap their geothermal reserves. Sixteen years later, Sinar Mas is building with that expertise in Indonesia, Barito has put a US$5-billion equity value on owning EDC, and First Gen is putting billions more into geothermal while saying it has no plans to sell.

The knowledge, its capital allocations suggest, is worth more kept than sold. – Rappler.com

Lala Rimando wrote about Philippine business, and managed newsrooms, including Newsbreak, ABS-CBN, Rappler, and Forbes, for over 25 years. She’s now based in La Union, taking care of her mom with dementia, and working on the multimedia biography of the late John Gokongwei.

World.title: Kazakhstan, Germany Set Sights on Deeper Economic Cooperation
World.content:
ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier held talks in Berlin on Sept. 29 to discuss the development of bilateral relations and prospects for further cooperation.

Tokayev thanked Steinmeier for the reception and invitation to visit Germany, describing the country as Kazakhstan’s key strategic partner in Europe. He said bilateral ties are based on mutual trust, respect and shared interests.

The two countries will mark the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year. Tokayev noted significant progress across a broad range of cooperation over the past three decades.

Steinmeier, in turn, highlighted Tokayev’s personal contribution to expanding cooperation between Kazakhstan and Germany. He said the visit would add momentum to bilateral relations and take them to a new level.

Economic cooperation takes a central place

The talks come as economic ties have become an important component of the Kazakhstan-Germany partnership. Earlier on Sept. 29, Tokayev met with heads of leading German business associations and financial institutions, where he proposed establishing a Kazakhstan-Germany Investment and Financial Platform to facilitate joint projects and investment.

During the visit, Tokayev also met with executives of major German companies, discussing transport and logistics, industrial localization, engineering, metallurgy and waste processing. Discussions included developing the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route, modernizing railway and logistics infrastructure, expanding manufacturing in Kazakhstan, developing engineering and service capabilities, and exploring potential projects in metal processing and waste management.

A visit at a new stage of relations

Tokayev’s Sept. 29-Oct. 1 visit includes meetings in Berlin and Munich and comes as Kazakhstan-Germany relations continue to expand politically and economically.

At the same time, the discussions have increasingly focused on moving from political dialogue and existing cooperation frameworks toward specific investment, industrial and infrastructure projects.

The meetings in Germany aim to strengthen this economic dimension of bilateral relations and expand opportunities for German companies in Kazakhstan and the wider Central Asian market.

World.title: C5+1 SI Conference Highlights AI Cooperation and Digital Growth in Central Asia
World.content:
ASTANA – Central Asia is seeking to turn its growing digital capabilities, energy resources and human capital into a stronger regional AI economy, with the United States offering support for digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and technology investment.

Officials and experts discussed the opportunities and challenges of building that ecosystem at the C5+1 SI Conference: Digital Innovation for Economic Growth, which opened Sept. 29 in Astana.

U.S. sees Central Asia as emerging AI hub

Mark Cameron,the deputy assistant secretary, Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs, U.S. Department of State, called on private-sector representatives to explore business opportunities in Central Asia, highlighting the region’s potential in the rapidly developing technology sector.

“This region is brimming with talent, ambition and untapped potential. We are here to support you, to open doors and to set every single company in this room up for success,” Cameron said.

He also highlighted the importance of making advanced technologies more accessible and understandable to the public.

“Super Intelligence (SI) is the future. It is reshaping economies, reshaping governments, reshaping the way our citizens live, work and connect with one another. And I believe, with complete confidence, that we as C5+1 countries are in the right place, at the right time and with the right partners to capitalize on the incredible momentum we have built on this issue,” Cameron said.

Cameron said the U.S. administration views Central Asia’s digital potential seriously and highlighted a $5 million U.S. foreign assistance commitment through CRDF Global to support cybersecurity and the digital sector in Central Asia.

The initiative is intended to strengthen cyber hygiene, cyber incident response, critical infrastructure protection, financial-sector security and cybersecurity policymaking.

Cameron also emphasized commitments made by the five Central Asian countries and the United States in Bishkek last spring to strengthen regional digital cooperation. These include efforts to unify digital frameworks and coordination mechanisms, harmonize personal data protection and intellectual property regimes in the IT sector, develop a coordinated approach to data center infrastructure and improve the business environment for cooperation with U.S. companies on SI.

He said greater investment in the Trans-Caspian Trade Route and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) could further strengthen regional economic integration.

“Central Asia is strategically positioned to be a vital hub for the flow of data and ideas. Trusted information and communication infrastructure will be essential to ensuring countries reap the benefits of new technologies and enhanced digital connectivity,” Cameron said.

Responding to a question from The Astana Times about areas of U.S.-Kazakhstan cooperation that could help build the infrastructure needed to develop domestic AI economies, Cameron highlighted data centers and trusted digital infrastructure as key priorities.

“Building the data centers and building the trusted infrastructure will give the American companies the confidence to be able to invest and expand their cooperation,” he said.

Cameron also pointed to Central Asia’s human capital, including its highly educated population and growing number of people with experience in AI and digital technologies.

“There is so much potential here. The region has a very educated population, a growing number of people working in IT, and several American universities working in partnership with Kazakh universities. That is helping to build the human infrastructure and create potential for future cooperation. Kazakhstan is really opening up possibilities for great future cooperation with the United States,” Cameron said.

Kazakhstan emphasizes regional cooperation

Bakhtiyar Mukhametkaliyev, vice minister of artificial intelligence and digital development of Kazakhstan, described Central Asia as a young region with significant economic and technological potential.

“Technology is changing very fast, and AI will change our economies, our industries and the way our governments work,” Mukhametkaliyev said.

He noted that several countries in the region are developing solutions with global potential and stressed the need for greater regional cooperation.

“Our task now is to build on this foundation, move faster and strengthen Central Asia’s position in the global technology market. To do this, we need to work together. We need to connect our infrastructure, talents and projects. And most importantly, our meetings should bring concrete results. Kazakhstan is open and ready for this work,” he said.

Responding to a question from The Astana Times, Mukhametkaliyev outlined several layers he considers essential for building an AI-driven economy. These include energy and water infrastructure, access to advanced chips and GPUs, information systems, high-quality data and AI agents.

“The first is energy infrastructure and water, because we need sufficient energy to create smart data centers. The second is access to chips and GPUs, which is one of the most important factors. The next is information systems, because if you don’t have a strong information system in your country, it becomes a major challenge,” he said.

He noted that high-quality data is another essential component and cautioned against focusing on AI agents without first developing the underlying infrastructure.

“Some countries are trying to implement AI agents first, but they do not necessarily bring additional economic benefits because AI agents need to work with your data, infrastructure and energy, and they need access to your databases. Only then can they provide information to support decision-making,” Mukhametkaliyev said.

Tajikistan proposes regional AI center

Hakim Ismoilzoda, first deputy director of Tajikistan’s Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies, highlighted infrastructure, connectivity and regional cooperation as key priorities for developing AI.

He said Tajikistan is revising its national AI strategy and plans to increase the target contribution of AI to GDP from 5% to 8%, covering 17 economic sectors.

Ismoilzoda also emphasized Tajikistan’s plans to dedicate 100 megawatts of green energy to AI data centers, with the goal of reaching 1 gigawatt by 2030.

“Without energy, without clean energy, without connectivity, it’s really difficult to develop digital technologies and specifically AI,” he said.

He pointed to the country’s IT Hub Dushanbe and plans to establish a Central Asian Regional AI Development Center as part of a broader regional approach to AI development.

“We are inviting all our partners, all our friends, including the U.S.-based companies and the U.S. government, to join this initiative,” Ismoilzoda said.

He highlighted that closer coordination among Central Asian countries could help create a larger regional market and attract investment.

World.title: Transport, Manufacturing and Recycling in Focus as Tokayev Meets German Companies
World.content:
ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev held a series of meetings with executives of major German companies during his official visit to Germany, discussing cooperation in transport and logistics, industrial localization, engineering, metallurgy and waste processing.

Speaking with Chairman of the Executive Board of Rhenus Group Tobias Bartz, Tokayev discussed the development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR), also known as the Middle Corridor. Tokayev called for joint efforts to develop a competitive route supported by modern ports, terminals, railways and digital services.

In a separate meeting, Tokayev highlighted the contribution of Deutsche Bahn to Kazakhstan’s railway development, including the joint project between DB Engineering & Consulting and Kazakhstan Temir Zholy to develop passenger rail services. He also stressed the importance of integrating Kazakh manufacturers into Deutsche Bahn’s supply chain, including through the necessary certification procedures.

Tokayev separately met Oliver Hermes, Chairman of the Executive Board of Wilo Group, a German technology company specializing in pumps and energy-efficient solutions for residential, public and industrial buildings. He called for deeper localization, including increasing the share of locally produced components, developing engineering and service capabilities, and expanding Kazakh suppliers’ participation. He also welcomed plans to establish a regional service and engineering center for pumping equipment in Alatau City.

President Tokayev also emphasized the metallurgical sector’s importance to Kazakhstan’s economy, discussing the reconstruction of Qarmet, one of the country’s major metallurgical enterprises, with Chairman of the Executive Board of D.A.R. Metall AG Christian Artner. They paid particular attention to a potential joint project for metal processing in Kazakhstan.

The meetings underscored Kazakhstan’s efforts to attract German expertise and investment across several sectors, while expanding local production, technology transfer and integration of Kazakh companies into international supply chains.

Commenting on the visit, experts highlight that the next stage of Kazakhstan-Germany economic cooperation will depend on whether high-level political commitments can translate into commercially viable projects. Stephan Meister, a German expert on Central Asia, pointed to the size of Kazakhstan’s domestic market as one consideration facing German companies, speaking with The Astana Times.

This means the visit’s significance may ultimately extend beyond the number of agreements announced. A stronger indication of deeper economic ties would be whether the existing framework leads to projects that create more value in Kazakhstan while giving German companies stronger commercial incentives to expand their presence.

Earlier on Sept. 29, Tokayev also met with heads of leading German business associations and financial institutions, where he proposed creating a Kazakhstan-Germany Investment and Financial Platform to facilitate investment and joint projects.

World.title: Moody’s Maintains Kazakhstan’s Baa1 Rating as Non-Oil Sectors Drive Growth
World.content:
ASTANA – Moody’s Ratings has affirmed Kazakhstan’s sovereign credit rating at Baa1 with a stable outlook, citing the country’s strong fiscal position, low government debt, high debt-servicing capacity and accumulated foreign-currency assets.

According to the agency, these factors give Kazakhstan flexibility in economic policymaking and a substantial buffer against external economic shocks, the Ministry of National Economy’s press service reported.

Moody’s noted that Kazakhstan’s economy continues to expand despite a decline in oil production, with manufacturing, construction, transport and other non-oil sectors making a significant contribution to GDP growth.

The agency expects continued investment in digital, transport and energy infrastructure to support medium-term economic growth and increase the complexity of the economy. Non-resource sectors are expected to remain the main drivers of economic expansion, according to Moody’s.

The agency also highlighted ongoing tax reforms as a factor that could strengthen Kazakhstan’s fiscal sustainability by broadening the government’s non-oil revenue base. Moody’s assessment indicates that the combination of economic diversification, tax reform and continued infrastructure investment is improving Kazakhstan’s fiscal prospects and creating conditions for further economic growth.

The agency said investments in digital, transport and energy infrastructure, alongside the expansion of non-oil sectors, would contribute to the economy’s continued diversification.

World.title: Tokayev Proposes Kazakhstan-Germany Investment and Financial Platform
World.content:
ASTANA – President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has proposed creating a Kazakhstan-Germany investment and financial platform to combine German and European capital with Kazakh co-financing, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms, as he outlined several priority areas for expanding economic cooperation between the two countries.

Tokayev made the proposal during his Sept. 29 meeting with leaders of leading German business associations and financial institutions, which opened his official visit to Germany. Addressing the participants, Tokayev emphasized the importance Kazakhstan attaches to its economic partnership with Germany, describing the country as one of Kazakhstan’s key European partners.

“Kazakh-German cooperation is an integral part of Kazakhstan’s engagement with the European Union, our largest trade and investment partner. We have come a long way together, but the potential of our economic partnership is far from exhausted. Kazakhstan is ready to take it to a qualitatively new level,” Tokayev said.

He highlighted Germany’s banking sector, engineering expertise and Mittelstand, the country’s network of small and medium-sized enterprises, as examples of strengths Kazakhstan seeks to incorporate into its own modernization and technological transformation.

Proposed investment and financial platform

Tokayev proposed establishing a Kazakhstan-Germany investment and financial platform that would bring together German and European capital with Kazakh co-financing, guarantees and risk-sharing mechanisms. According to him, the Baiterek holding would provide project structuring, while German export credit and investment insurance institutions could participate alongside international financial organizations already operating in Kazakhstan.

President Tokayev also noted that Kazakhstan’s development institutions play an active role in financing the national economy. Last year, these institutions provided $20 billion in support.

He also said the Development Bank of Kazakhstan financed major projects in industry, energy and transport infrastructure with support from German financial institutions, attracting more than $1.2 billion from Deutsche Bank, Helaba, LBBW, Commerzbank, KfW and other organizations.

Tokayev also told the German business community that S&P recently upgraded Kazakhstan’s sovereign rating to BBB with a stable outlook, while Fitch confirmed the same assessment.

Focus on critical materials and energy

Critical materials were identified as another priority area for bilateral cooperation. Kazakhstan is interested in working with Germany’s Raw Materials Fund and promoting projects eligible for UFK guarantees, Tokayev said. Such cooperation could help secure reliable supplies of raw materials for German industry.

He also highlighted opportunities to modernize Kazakhstan’s energy and industrial sectors, including through renewable energy and green hydrogen projects. He said there was significant potential for cooperation between the European Investment Bank and the Development Bank of Kazakhstan with the participation of German capital.

Kazakhstan-Germany partnership in AI and digital technologies

Digital innovation and artificial intelligence were also identified as areas for deeper cooperation. Tokayev invited German companies to apply their expertise in data center technologies, energy efficiency, cloud infrastructure and cybersecurity in Kazakhstan. Fintech was highlighted as another promising field.

“The high level of development of Kazakhstan’s digital financial ecosystem creates opportunities for the development of advanced payment solutions and tokenization technologies in the domestic market, with their subsequent scaling across the region,” Tokayev said.

He also noted that Kazakhstan has developed what he described as an advanced digital and financial ecosystem in the region over the past decade.

Alatau City as potential investment gateway

Tokayev also presented the development of Alatau City as another potential area for German investment. According to him, the project is envisioned as a smart city designed around the requirements of the digital era and could serve as a link between German institutional capital and investment opportunities in Kazakhstan.

“This project represents the first smart city in Central Asia, initially designed with all the requirements of the digital era in mind. It can become a practical bridge between German institutional capital and Kazakhstan’s investment opportunities,” Tokayev said.

Expanding Kazakhstan-Germany economic ties

The meeting also focused on combining German financial resources, expertise and risk-management instruments with Kazakhstan’s resource base and transport potential. Tokayev said Kazakhstan seeks to become a reliable partner for Germany in Central Asia and across the Eurasian space.

He stressed that closer cooperation should not be limited to increasing capital inflows but should also include the joint creation of new industries and long-term sources of economic growth.

Tokayev assured German investors that Kazakhstan would continue to provide favorable and predictable conditions, protect investors’ rights, and support strategically important projects.

World.title: Central Asian Countries Discuss Common Digital Economy and AI Rules
World.content:
ASTANA – Representatives of Central Asian business associations, IT companies, experts and government bodies gathered in Astana on Sept. 28 to discuss proposals to make the region’s five digital markets more compatible and create easier conditions for technology companies to expand across Central Asia.

The regional roundtable was held with the support of Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development as part of the B5+1 Cycle. Discussions focused on initiatives proposed by the business community for inclusion in the Regional Business Agenda for 2027.

Toward compatible digital systems

A central proposal discussed at the meeting was a draft Agreement on Cooperation among Central Asian States in Digital Policy and Artificial Intelligence Governance. The proposed framework does not call for identical digital legislation or a supranational regulator. Instead, it envisages maintaining national legislation and digital sovereignty while gradually making countries’ legal and digital systems compatible.

The areas identified for closer alignment include electronic document management and digital identification, personal data protection, cybersecurity and AI regulation.

The initiative also proposes creating conditions for the mutual recognition of electronic documents, electronic signatures and digital identification tools. According to the proposal, this could reduce administrative and legal barriers for businesses providing digital services across borders.

“Our task is not to create another layer of regulation. We need to build digital bridges between the countries of Central Asia,” said Chair of the Board of TechnoWomen Aziza Shuzheeva.

Common principles for responsible AI

Another proposal presented at the roundtable was a draft Code of Ethics for the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Central Asia. The document would establish common ethical principles for the five countries while maintaining the priority of national legislation. It is designed as a recommendation and does not envisage a supranational AI regulator, mandatory certification or accreditation of AI systems.

One core principle is that AI can assist people in making decisions but should not replace human responsibility.

The draft proposes that when an AI-assisted decision significantly affects a person’s rights or interests, an algorithm should not make the decision alone. It also outlines proposed rights to know when a person is interacting with AI, receive an understandable explanation of an AI-generated result and request human review.

The document identifies several practices as unacceptable, including harmful manipulation, exploitation of vulnerable groups, discriminatory practices, unlawful use of personal data, and the use of synthetic content for fraud or harm.

Focus on Central Asian languages

The proposed code also addresses the region’s linguistic and cultural diversity. Participants proposed developing regional language resources and datasets to improve AI systems’ ability to work with Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Uzbek, Tajik, Turkmen and other regional languages.

The draft also includes provisions related to protection against algorithmic discrimination, gender equality and greater participation of women in the development, deployment and assessment of AI systems. Particular attention is proposed for the impact of AI technologies on children, older people, people with disabilities and residents of rural areas.

Six business proposals

The initiatives discussed at the meeting build on consultations the Regional IT & AI Working Group conducted with entrepreneurs, industry associations and experts across Central Asia.

During the previous cycle, the consultation process involved business communities representing more than 60 companies and organizations from Central Asia and the United States, including Meta, Mastercard and Google.

The broader objective is to encourage international technology companies to view Central Asia not as five separate markets but as an increasingly interconnected digital region with a population of more than 80 million. Proposed mechanisms include creating a permanent regional platform for dialogue between governments and the private sector, allowing businesses to participate early in discussions on digitalization and AI regulations.

Participants also discussed strengthening engagement with global technology companies, cloud providers, telecommunications operators and investors to identify regulatory and infrastructure barriers to investment in the region.

Building a regional technology market

The roundtable results are expected to contribute to the development of the B5+1 Regional Business Agenda for 2027. The long-term objective discussed at the meeting is to make it easier for startups and technology companies originating in Astana, Tashkent, Bishkek, Dushanbe or Ashgabat to expand into neighboring markets.

The proposed approach would allow companies to operate across a more compatible regional digital environment while preserving each Central Asian country’s national legislation and digital sovereignty.

World.title: Kazakhstan to Develop New Container Routes Linking Central Asia and Europe
World.content:
ASTANA – A Kazakh infrastructure developer and investor SEMURG INVEST and MEDLOG Poti, a logistics operator and part of the global MSC Group, have signed a sale and purchase agreement to establish a strategic partnership in Sarzha Logistics. The partnership aims to expand container and multimodal freight flows across Central Asia and strengthen connections to Türkiye and European markets.

After completing the transaction, MEDLOG and SEMURG will form an equal partnership in Sarzha Logistics, which will operate container cargo flows in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the Kyrgyz Republic and Tajikistan.

Focus on Middle Corridor connectivity

The partnership comes as Kazakhstan and Central Asian countries seek to diversify export routes and develop more resilient connections between East and West. Sarzha Logistics will combine SEMURG’s local infrastructure and project development capabilities with MEDLOG’s international logistics network. The cooperation may cover logistics terminals, dry ports, railway infrastructure and other intermodal facilities.

“Kazakhstan is becoming increasingly important in East-West trade and regional supply chains. Through this partnership, we see an opportunity to develop new container and multimodal cargo flows connecting Central Asia through the Caspian and Georgia with Türkiye, Europe and our wider global network,” MEDLOG Poti Managing Director Mukhran Dekanadze said.

According to Dekanadze, MEDLOG’s presence in Georgia, MSC’s global shipping network and SEMURG’s infrastructure at Kuryk provide a basis for developing integrated logistics solutions along the Middle Corridor.

SEMURG INVEST General Director Nurzhan Marabayev said the partnership reflects growing interest among international operators and investors in establishing a long-term presence in Kazakhstan.

“International companies need not only an attractive market. They need local partners capable of investing, developing projects and implementing them in practice,” Marabayev said.

Sarzha to expand cargo-handling capacity

The partnership will rely on SEMURG’s infrastructure at Kuryk port on the Caspian Sea. The Sarzha Multifunctional Maritime Terminal cluster is planned to handle up to 5 million tonnes of cargo annually, including container capacity of up to 110,000 TEUs per year.

Sarzha is being developed as a multimodal port, logistics and industrial cluster on Kazakhstan’s Caspian coast, combining maritime terminals with logistics facilities, railway and road infrastructure. The project is intended to provide Kazakhstan and Central Asian countries with additional cargo-handling capacity and strengthen their access to markets in Türkiye and Europe.

World.title: Kazakh Olympic Champion Shaidorov Rises to Second in World Figure Skating Rankings
World.content:
ASTANA – Kazakhstan’s Mikhail Shaidorov has climbed to second place in the updated International Skating Union (ISU) world rankings with 4,193 points, marking the highest position of his career.

The rankings are led by United States skater Ilia Malinin with 4,590 points, while Japan’s Yuma Kagiyama is third with 4,123 points.

Shaidorov’s rise in the rankings follows his bronze-medal finish at the ISU Challenger Series Memorial Ondrej Nepela in Bratislava, Slovakia. The tournament marked the Kazakh skater’s first international competition of the 2026/27 season and his first international start since the 2026 Winter Olympic Games.

Shaidorov scored 272.75 points overall, earning 95.98 points in the short program and 176.77 points in the free skating program.

Russia’s Evgeni Semenenko, competing as a neutral athlete, won the tournament with 292.09 points, while Italy’s Daniel Grassl took second place with 278.80 points.

The second-place ranking represents Shaidorov’s highest-ever position in the ISU world rankings.

World.title: Abkhazia and Russia agree to mutually recognise customs inspection results
World.content:
Abkhazia and Russia have agreed to mutually recognise the results of customs inspections. The agreement is expected to speed up the clearance of goods at the Russian border on the Psou River.

Negotiations on the agreement took more than four years. Russia’s Federal Customs Service and Abkhazia’s Customs Committee signed the relevant protocol on 25 September.

The protocol provides for the electronic exchange of information on customs inspection results. This means that if one side has already inspected goods or a vehicle, the other side can use the results of that inspection in certain cases instead of conducting it again.

Abkhazia’s Customs Committee said the new mechanism should reduce border crossing times and ease pressure on checkpoints.

“This is particularly important during the holiday and citrus seasons, when passenger and vehicle traffic increases. We expect the new electronic cooperation mechanisms to shorten the time needed to complete the necessary procedures and improve the capacity of border checkpoints,” said Customs Committee head Otar Khetsia.

Previously, customs officials from both Abkhazia and Russia inspected each shipment separately. Disputes often arose when one side questioned the documents provided by the cargo owner and required the entire shipment to be unloaded. This caused queues at the border, much to the frustration of cargo owners.

Abkhaz officials say that the mutual recognition of customs inspection results is standard international practice and does not infringe on the sovereignty of either side.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.
